8d63d933f7859a14: PUTRAJAYA: The Madani government has increased the allocation for religious affairs to RM3.1 billion under the 2027 Budget to strengthen Islamic development, including the empowerment of religious educational institutions and safeguarding the welfare of religious personnel nationwide.

Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said 85.4 per cent of the allocation was for operating expenditure, while the remaining 14.6 per cent was set aside for development expenditure.
He said the increase reflected the government's commitment to implementing a more comprehensive agenda to elevate the stature of Islam and benefit society.

"The Madani government continues to place special emphasis on this agenda by allocating RM200 million for sekolah agama rakyat (community religious schools), tahfiz institutions and sekolah pondok (traditional Islamic boarding schools) registered with the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia (Jakim).
"The scope of assistance has also been expanded to cover the operating costs of these institutions," he said in a statement today.

Zulkifli said the government would also provide a special contribution of RM750 each to 70,000 religious personnel, including Kelas Al-Quran dan Fardu Ain (KAFA) teachers, takmir teachers, imams, bilals, tok siaks, nojas and marbuts, in recognition of their contributions to the community.
He said 500 KAFA teachers who teach students with special needs, including those who use sign language or the Braille Quran, would receive a special monthly incentive of RM150.

"The well-being of those who enliven the Houses of Allah is further supported by a special government allocation that fully covers Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) contributions for 40,000 imam, bilal, tok siak, mosque staff and takmir teachers.

"The Pilgrims Fund Board (Tabung Haji) serves as the implementing agency, ensuring continuous social security protection and providing peace of mind to these individuals as they serve the ummah," he said.

In a related development, Zulkifli said amendments to the Road Transport Act requiring drivers under the influence of alcohol or drugs to compensate victims or their families contained elements consistent with the Islamic legal concept of diyat, or financial compensation.
He said the concept recognised the right of victims or their heirs to receive compensation for harm caused by another person's actions.

He said the government was also strengthening the halal industry by offering matching grants of up to RM5,000 to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) seeking halal certification for the first time.
A separate grant of RM25,000 would be available to empower halal-certified MSMEs in high-potential sectors, including cosmetics and pharmaceuticals, he added.

In the Islamic education sector, he said Jakim and the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC) had initiated a collaboration to provide digital devices and skills training to teachers and students at more than 300 pondok schools nationwide.

Zulkifli said the initiatives reflected the government's approach of focusing not only on economic and infrastructure development but also on nurturing a knowledgeable, ethical and prosperous society.

"This Budget framework is formulated based on a philosophy that aspires to reach for the skies while remaining firmly rooted on the ground. We aim to elevate the nation's economy and the stature of Islam to the pinnacle of success, guided by a far-sighted vision," he said.
He added that the government's priorities and policy implementation would remain grounded in reality, with the ultimate aim of safeguarding the welfare and well-being of Malaysians.
TAGS: Zulkifli Hasan, Budget 2027, Islamic teachings, education, welfare

2d3a21cf9ecaac00: KUALA LUMPUR: Fires in Indonesia that have sent toxic smoke and disrupted daily life across Southeast Asia have triggered the highest-level alert by the regional bloc's meteorological monitor.
The months-long pollution spell has closed schools, fuelled a surge in respiratory conditions and restricted outdoor activities in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and East Timor.

"This thing needs to stop," Zul Hafiz, a 39-year-old teacher cycling from the Malaysian city of Shah Alam to the capital, told AFP on Saturday, calling on the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) to take action.

The 11-country organisation's Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) said in a notice on its website on Friday that it had activated "Alert Level 3 for the Southern Asean region" – the highest rung of a four-tiered alert system.

The alert level is triggered when there is a "high risk of severe transboundary haze in the region" and is reserved for widespread moderate to dense smoke haze, observed over two or more consecutive days.
The ASMC has already issued two Level 3 alerts this year, according to its website.
Singapore ranked second on IQAir's live ranking of the world's most polluted major cities behind Baghdad on Saturday, with Kuala Lumpur third. All readings showed "very hazardous" levels."
'Irresponsible behaviour'
Indonesia said Saturday it had been using dry ice at one of South Sumatra province's main airports in an attempt to disperse the haze.
The country's national disaster mitigation agency said that 2.4 tonnes of dry ice were dispersed by plane.
"The smoke not only reduces visibility and disrupts aircraft operations but also affects residents' health," the agency warned.
The haze has disrupted life across Southeast Asia, sparking fresh calls for action from those affected.
"It's a bit unfair on Malaysia because of the irresponsible behaviour of our neighbouring country," Khairul Azhar, a 33-year-old bank officer told AFP in Kuala Lumpur.
"This is affecting our weekend routine – not just for us but many Malaysians," he said.

In Indonesia's Palangkaraya – part of the epicentre of the fires where thick haze turned the skies into apocalyptic shades of yellow and orange – residents said they were suffering from its effects on Saturday.
"The haze has a big impact on us, especially on health and the economy, with our income decreasing," said Marzuki, a 38-year-old mechanic who, like many in Indonesia, goes by only one name.
"Right now the economy is already very difficult, and the haze just makes it worse," he told AFP, adding that this year's situation was worse than even previous major bouts of haze in 2015.
"Hopefully it rains soon, the fires go out, and the smoke disappears so that activities can return to normal and it’s easier to earn a living again," he said.
'What else to do?'
Joko, 51, a construction worker, said he had no choice but to keep on working, or he would lose out on income.

"The thick smoke, when inhaled, makes it hard to breathe and stings the eyes, but what else can you do? This is how we earn a living," Joko said, explaining he had no fixed income and relied on daily wage jobs.
In East Timor, unhealthy air pollution persisted on Saturday, including in the capital Dili, according to IQAir.
Authorities warned that the situation may worsen on Saturday, and schools were closed.
Singapore said Friday it would issue warnings to seven companies in Indonesia it identified as responsible for the fires.
Philippines foreign department spokesman for Asean issues, Dominic Xavier Imperial, said Friday that the haze would be discussed at upcoming meetings ahead of a November Asean summit in Manila.
0e015b2e07c45d78: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Alien fish account for 95 per cent of fish recorded in Tasik Ampang Hilir, posing a serious threat to the balance of Malaysia’s freshwater ecosystem.

Agriculture and Food Security Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Isham Ishak said mitigation efforts needed to be strengthened through data-driven approaches, community education and strategic cooperation involving the government, private sector and non-governmental organisations.

He warned that releasing pet fish into lakes, dams and public waterways when they grow too large or become difficult to care for could harm aquatic biodiversity and threaten the survival of local species.

“If we do not educate, this matter will become a culture that is difficult to curb and will become a long-term problem,” he said at the “Program Kelestarian Perikanan Darat: Mitigasi Memburu Ikan Asing” at Tasik Ampang Hilir here today.
The alien fish-catching programme, conducted from 2022 to 2025, recorded a total catch of 19.74 tonnes, highlighting the need to address the spread of these species more seriously.

Isham said measures included increasing efforts to catch alien fish, releasing local fish fry to help restore the balance of fish populations and expanding public education to discourage people from releasing pet fish into public waters.
He said the ministry was also reviewing ways to tighten existing regulations, including the possibility of banning certain fish species identified as threats to local ecosystems.
Agrobank released 1,400 native fish fry into the lake to support the conservation of local species, comprising 1,100 baung and 300 lampam sungai.
Records from the Malaysian Department of Fisheries showed that 146 of the 154 fish recorded in Tasik Ampang Hilir were alien species, while only eight were native species.

Agrobank chief development officer Ahmad Arif Abu Bakar said efforts to restore the balance between native and alien fish populations needed to be supported by greater public awareness and education on the importance of protecting Malaysia’s biodiversity.
“The public needs to understand their responsibility in maintaining the ecosystem, including not releasing pet fish into rivers or lakes when the fish grow larger,” he said.

The programme brought together about 250 participants from seven agencies and organisations, with activities including catching alien fish using seine nets, cast nets, fishing lines and fish traps. — Bernama
893ac98bf3bd3318: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 17 — A total of 202.3 hectares of land have been reclaimed at Silicon Island since reclamation works began in September 2023, marking progress in the development of Penang’s next economic growth hub as of October 2026.

Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the development was envisioned to complement the state’s semiconductor industry while attracting investments in advanced technology, research and development, and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven innovation.

“The early launch of the Silicon Island Experience Centre offers visitors a closer look at our vision for a new growth hub that will complement Penang’s semiconductor industry and attract investments in advanced technology, research and development, and AI-driven innovation,” he said in a Facebook post today.
He said Silicon Island was also expected to create quality jobs, develop local talent and benefit surrounding communities, with sustainability remaining a key priority.

Chow said the state government hoped that, with the right support and strategic partnerships, it could take Penang’s economy to the next level and build a stronger, greener future for generations to come.

In a separate statement, Silicon Island Development Sdn Bhd said the Silicon Island Experience Centre was now open to government agencies, investors, local communities and strategic partners to help them better understand the 931-hectare development.

It said the 2,500-square-foot facility featured an interactive LED scale model showcasing key components of the development, including a 283-hectare Green Tech Park, commercial precincts, transit corridors and more than 110 kilometres of dedicated cycling and pedestrian paths.
Built at a cost of RM2.5 million, the centre was completed in four months.

Silicon Island is designed as a smart city with a five-diamond Low Carbon City accreditation, with its development expected to support Penang’s long-term economic growth while incorporating sustainable urban planning.

Penang Infrastructure Corporation Sdn Bhd chief executive officer and Silicon Island Development chairman Datuk Seri Farizan Darus said reclamation works began in September 2023, with 202.3 hectares of land physically reclaimed as of October 2026.
“Physical progress on the RM420 million Pan Island Link 2A contract is also moving smoothly.

“We are targeting the opening of the first section of the marine bridge connecting Jalan Permatang Damar Laut directly to Silicon Island by December 2028, leading towards full completion by June 2029,” he said. — Bernama
b5fe380f4281fc89: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) has denied allegations that the action against former Setiawangsa member of parliament Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad by the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) over a khalwat (proximity) case was an act of persecution or a "frame-up".
MAIS chairman Datuk Salehuddin Saidin said JAIS acted based on an official complaint and in accordance with established legal procedures, without manipulating the situation to target any individual.

"The suggestion that the religious department was involved in manipulation or anything of the sort is entirely untrue. We have a legal obligation...when a complaint is lodged, we are required to conduct a thorough investigation.
"Rest assured, JAIS will carry out the investigation as diligently as possible, and if there is clear evidence, we will proceed with charges in court," he said.

He was speaking to reporters after the 2026 Gathering of Accredited Religious Teachers in Selangor at the Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Silver Jubilee Hall here. Also present was Selangor Mufti Datuk Dr Anhar Opir.
Salehuddin said the case was made public to clarify that Syariah laws were enforced fairly, regardless of the background or influence of the individual under investigation.
He called on the public to allow JAIS sufficient time and space to complete its investigation and refrain from speculation that could compromise the fairness of the legal process.

"We cannot pass judgment while the investigation is still incomplete. We must act fairly and carry out our duties in accordance with the regulations. If we were to act outside these regulations, we ourselves would be subject to accusations," he said.

Nik Nazmi, on Instagram, had confirmed that he was one of two people detained by JAIS in Petaling Jaya last Thursday over allegations of khalwat. He said he was prepared to cooperate with any legal proceedings.
Earlier today, PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari dismissed claims that it was weaponising khalwat claims against rival political leaders to weaken opponents.
"We have better things to do than set up khalwat traps," he was quoted as saying.
Nik Nazmi and Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli had left PKR, vacating their Setiawangsa and Pandan parliamentary seats to set up the independent party Bersama.

Meanwhile, on a separate case involving a local youth suspected of participating in the rituals of another religion, Salehuddin said preliminary findings suggested that the individual's actions were, so far, a matter of personal belief.
However, he said JAIS was examining various forms of digital evidence, including social media posts concerning rituals at Batu Caves that had been linked to other belief systems.

"The public must understand that when we intend to take legal action in court, we must ensure that all evidence is authentic. We are aware that material could potentially be superimposed or generated via AI (artificial intelligence); therefore, we have experts who can verify its authenticity.
"Regarding the issue of apostasy, we cannot impose penalties without conducting a thorough investigation. We certainly consult with the relevant authorities before taking action against anyone.
"A comprehensive investigation must be carried out first," he said.

On Oct 13, JAIS director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad said a man who went viral over allegations that he had performed rituals of another religion, which is in breach of Syariah law, had been detained alongside his mother in Kuala Lumpur to assist in an investigation under Sections 4 and 10 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995.
167191bca6f473ce: SHAH ALAM: Majlis Agama Islam Selangor (Mais) menafikan dakwaan bahawa penahanan bekas Ahli Parlimen Setiawangsa Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad berhubung kes khalwat oleh Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor (Jais) pada Khamis lepas ialah satu tindakan penganiayaan atau perangkap.

Pengerusi Salehuddin Saidin menegaskan agensi penguatkuasaan bertindak sepenuhnya berlandaskan aduan rasmi yang diterima, serta mengikut undang-undang yang ditetapkan tanpa memanipulasi keadaan demi mengenakan mana-mana pihak.

"Bila dikatakan seolah-olah jabatan agama terlibat dalam manipulasi dan sebagainya, ini tidak benar sama sekali. Kami juga ada tanggungjawab mengikut undang-undang apabila aduan dibuat, kami perlu melakukan siasatan secara menyeluruh.

"Jadi, percayalah Jais akan menjalankan siasatan sebaik mungkin dan kalau ada keterangan jelas kita akan buat pertuduhan di mahkamah," katanya ketika ditemui selepas majlis Ijtimak Pemegang Tauliah Mengajar Negeri Selangor 2026.

Mengulas tindakan memaklumkan kes berkenaan kepada umum, Salehuddin berkata perkara itu dibuat bagi memberikan pencerahan bahawa undang-undang syariah dilaksanakan secara adil tanpa mengira latar belakang atau pengaruh individu yang disiasat.

Sehubungan itu, beliau menggesa masyarakat supaya memberikan ruang secukupnya kepada Jais bagi melengkapkan prosedur siasatan serta mengelakkan sebarang spekulasi liar yang boleh menjejaskan keadilan proses perundangan.

"Kita tidak boleh menjatuhkan hukum selagi siasatan belum lengkap, kita perlu berlaku adil dan melaksanakan tanggungjawab mengikut peraturan. Sekiranya dilakukan tanpa peraturan dan sebagainya, kita juga akan ditohmah," katanya.

Terdahulu, Nik Nazmi dalam kenyataan di Instagram mengesahkan beliau ialah seorang daripada dua individu yang ditahan Jais atas dakwaan berkhalwat di Petaling Jaya, Khamis lepas dan bersedia memberikan kerjasama untuk sebarang proses perundangan.
f7785d0154c9441a: KUALA TERENGGANU: Police issued 447 summonses and seized 125 motorcycles during 'Op Samseng Jalanan 2026', a two-day operation conducted at two locations in Kuala Terengganu.
District police chief assistant commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the action followed inspections on motorcycles believed to have been involved in the Gen-Y Event 2026 celebrations.

He said the offences detected included missing side mirrors, failure to display a valid motor vehicle licence, expired motor vehicle licences, non-compliant number plates and modified motorcycle exhausts.

"The operation was conducted on Oct 16 and 17 following public complaints about a group of youths riding motorcycles dangerously and causing noise in the Kampung Padang Midin residential area and Kuala Terengganu city centre.

"A total of 125 motorcycles were seized for various offences under Section 64 of the Road Transport Act 1987. The operation was carried out from midnight until the early hours of the morning," he said in a statement today.
Police advised the public to comply with traffic laws and refrain from dangerous riding, which poses a risk to themselves and other road users.

71219d8232507ff2: KYIV: Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky said Saturday that US President Donald Trump's decision to block sanctions on Moscow only "rewards" Russia's Vladimir Putin and warned Moscow was trying to deprive "millions" of Ukrainians of heat and electricity before winter.
Amid a clash with the Ukrainian wartime leader, Trump signed an executive order that waived sweeping US sanctions targeting Russia's energy revenues.

The decision came despite Russia increasing strikes on Ukraine – especially its capital, Kyiv - in the fifth year of its offensive, which has killed hundreds of thousands of people and displaced millions.

The Lindsey Graham Act – named after the deceased US senator who sponsored the bill – targeted Russia's energy and defence sectors, as well as Putin and the so-called "shadow fleet" of tankers used by Moscow to circumvent Western sanctions.
Zelensky said the decision came the same day as Russia attacked 15 critical power generation facilities across Ukraine in "one of the largest" attacks on Ukraine's energy grid.
"It is important that everyone in America also sees what is really happening," he said on social media.
The Lindsey Graham Act, he said, was "supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end", adding that the act "could have helped enormously – and still can!"
"A US sanctions blackout, easing pressure on the aggressor, financial rewards for Putin – all of this only encourages him to keep attacking," he warned.
The Ukrainian leader said Russia wanted to cause a "blackout" in Ukraine ahead of winter: "Russia is trying to leave millions of our people without electricity and heating."
He called on allies to keep up pressure on Moscow to "stop this."
Last winter saw hundreds of thousands in Ukraine consistently without heat and electricity in freezing temperatures.
A day after Trump waived the sanctions, causing Europe and Kyiv to worry which side of the war the White House is on, Ukraine said at least two people were killed in Russian air strikes.
Officials said one person was killed in the southern city of Kherson in an attack that also wounded 22 people, including two children, and that another was killed in the northeastern city of Sumy.
Russia hails Trump move as 'historic'
The Kremlin and Putin have not yet reacted to Trump, but several Russian officials celebrated the move as a win.
"The Trump administration's suspension of the Graham Act is an important and truly historic moment," Kirill Dmitriev, a Putin envoy, said on social media.
Dmitriev said the act would have caused "serious damage first and foremost to the US economy and global markets".
Trump's waiver comes after he struck a deal with Putin to ease existing sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel onto global markets.
He announced the executive order Friday, shortly after Putin appeared in military uniform and said Moscow aims to capture the rest of eastern Ukraine.
US-led talks to end the war in Ukraine have not led to a breakthrough. Both Putin and Zelensky have frustrated Trump in the past with a lack of progress in halting the grinding war.

Zelensky had rallied his allies Friday on a visit to Brussels for a European Union summit, urging them to keep financing Ukraine's fight and insisting he was standing up for his country amid the row with Trump.
Putin vows more
Ukraine has been struggling to shoot down Russian missiles and has been left scrambling to boost defences ahead of winter.
Russia controls large swathes of eastern and southern Ukraine, and Putin has repeatedly said Moscow intends to seize the rest of eastern Ukraine by force.
"On the whole I see a positive trend in the operations of the troop groupings," Putin told army leaders Friday, dressed in military attire.
"Undoubtedly, one of the main objectives remains the liberation of the Donetsk People's Republic," he added, using the Kremlin's name for the eastern Donetsk region.
European leaders put on a show of unity with Zelensky Friday as he grappled with Trump.
"This is no time to withdraw the support to Ukraine. This is no time to relieve Russia's sanctions," said European Council chief Antonio Costa.
"Now it is time to increase our support, to increase our pressure."
17a5b67f97b6decb: JERTIH: A man and his son who went missing on Thursday while searching for medicinal roots in a forest near the La Hot Spring recreational area in Hulu Besut were found safe at noon today.
The two men, Adam Adnan, 25, and his father Adnan Mohamad, 57, were found by a search and rescue (SAR) team at 12.40pm, about 3km from the operation's command post.
Besut police chief superintendent Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim said they were brought out of the forest at 2.45pm via the Lata Kolam Air Deru recreational area.
"The two men were found weak after going without food for three days while lost in the forest.
"They were assisted down by the rescue team before being taken by a Civil Defence Force (CDF) ambulance to Besut Hospital for treatment," he told reporters today.
It was reported earlier today that the father and son had gone missing after entering the forest to search for medicinal roots.

e5e391cd8b7d8eab: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang Hindu Endowments Board (PHEB) has given one-off financial aid to families affected by the Aug 26 Nepal-Tibet border tragedy.
PHEB deputy chairman Senator Dr Lingeshwaran R. Arunasalam said four families from Penang were identified, with three accepting the RM5,000 assistance.

Speaking at the aid handover ceremony, Lingeshwaran urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and the federal government to consider similar one-off assistance for all affected Malaysian families nationwide.
Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying, who attended the event, extended her condolences to the families and commended PHEB's welfare efforts.

She said her ministry, through the National Welfare Foundation, was providing RM500 to each affected family, while her office was contributing an additional RM1,000 per family. Emotional distress and psychosocial support were also available through the Talian Kasih helpline at 15999.
Bukit Gelugor MP Ramkarpal Singh contributed RM5,000 to one affected family from his constituency.

PHEB chairman RSN Rayer urged authorities to expedite the legal declaration of death, issuance of death certificates and other official documentation to help families settle insurance claims, property transfers and urgent financial matters.
9ee0be884f7cc76c: PETALING JAYA: Dua peguam menggesa kerajaan agar membawa pulang pembunuh yang disabitkan kesalahan, Sirul Azhar Umar, dari Australia bagi membuka semula kes pembunuhan warga Mongolia, Altantuya Shaaribuu, yang 'belum selesai'. Altantuya ditembak dan mayatnya diletupkan pada 2006.
Bekas peguam negara, Tommy Thomas, berkata Malaysia hanya memerlukan 30 minit untuk memastikan Sirul dapat diektradisi. Sirul melarikan diri ke Australia pada 2015.

"Malaysia hanya perlu memberikan aku janji kepada Australia bahawa Sirul tidak akan berdepan hukuman mati sekembalinya dia. Menteri luar, menteri dalam negeri dan peguam negara mesti duduk bersama dan menulis surat kepada rakan sejawat di Australia," kata Thomas.

"Ia semudah itu -- surat yang boleh ditulis dalam masa setengah jam. Saya fikir tiada iltizam politik. Mereka lebih suka ia menjadi sebahagian daripada sejarah dan mahu semua orang melupakannya. Tetapi ia tidak boleh dilupakan."

Kes Altantuya menjadi perhatian apabila perincian yang terdedah mengaitkan wanita itu dengan Abdul Razak Baginda, seorang pembantu kepada menteri pertahanan ketika itu, Najib Razak, spekulasi mengenai penglibatannya dalam perjanjian kapal selam antara Perancis dan Malaysia, serta mesej antara Razak dan Musa Safri, seorang lagi pegawai pembantu kepada Najib.

Thomas dan peguam, Sangeet Kaur Deo, yang mewakili keluarga Altantuya, berkata ekstradisi Sirul akan membolehkan pihak berkuasa Malaysia mengesahkan dakwaan Sirul mengenai pembunuhan itu, yang dibuat dalam akuan berkanun semasa dia ditahan oleh imigresen Australia.

Bercakap kepada Al Jazeera dalam dokumentari 'Murder in Malaysia – Justice for Altantuya' yang ditayangkan hari ini, Thomas dan Sangeet berkata dakwaan Sirul dalam akuan berkanun -- dan dakwaan oleh rakan subahatnya, Azilah Hadri, dalam akuan berasingan -- mesti disahkan bagi membuka semula kes tersebut.
Thomas dan Sangeet berkata dua orang itu patut berdepan tindakan kerana membuat akuan palsu sekiranya dakwaan mereka tidak benar.

Sirul melarikan diri ke Australia untuk memohon suaka sebelum Mahkamah Persekutuan menjatuhkan hukuman mati ke atasnya. Permohonan suakanya ditolak pada 2019 dan dia ditahan sehingga tahun 2023, apabila dia dibebaskan ke dalam masyarakat; bagaimanapun, dia tidak boleh dihantar pulang ke Malaysia kerana undang-undang Australia menghalang penghantaran pulang sekiranya pemohon akan berdepan hukuman mati.
Susulan pemansuhan hukuman mati mandatori di Malaysia dan hukuman Azilah diringankan kepada 40 tahun penjara, Thomas berkata tiada sebab Sirul tidak boleh diektradisi.
Tiada jawapan daripada AG
Sangeet berkata beliau telah menulis surat kepada peguam negara tetapi tidak menerima sebarang maklum balas. "Adalah menjadi kewajipan mereka untuk menjawab," katanya.
Jika Sirul berbohong dalam afidavit maka tindakan patut diambil, katanya. "Jika dia betul, sesuatu juga patut dilakukan. Tugas saya hanya meminta ia disiasat," katanya kepada Al Jazeera.

Beliau berkata keluarga Altantuya ingin Malaysia dan Australia mencari jalan penyelesaian yang sah di sisi undang-undang melalui mahkamah dan diplomasi, agar kebertanggungjawaban akhirnya ditegakkan. "Kita mesti meleraikan kebuntuan ini, kerana kebuntuan itu suatu ketidakadilan."
Beliau berkata soalan yang paling ketara ialah mengapa Azilah, seorang komando polis, menerima arahan daripada Razak yang bukannya pegawai atasannya. "Soalan itu belum terjawab dan patut disiasat."

Sangeet mengambil maklum bahawa Razak, yang dibebaskan daripada pertuduhan bersubahat dalam pembunuhan Altantuya, mempunyai peluang untuk menyatakan secara bersumpah bahawa kedua-dua lelaki itu bertindak bersendirian, semasa perbicaraan saman sivil yang difailkan oleh bapa Altantuya, Shaariibuu.
"Beliau memilih untuk tidak mengambil peluang itu."
Mesej kepada Musa Safri
Dokumentari itu mendedahkan mesej teks yang dihantar oleh Razak kepada pembantu Najib, Musa, pada malam sebelum pembunuhan Altantuya.
Pada pukul 9.35 malam, Razak menulis: "Did you get my SMS about wanting to meet at DPM’s office?" Tiga minit kemudian: "When will you be there? I can drop by in the morning. Tks."

Razak mencadangkan pertemuan di pejabat timbalan perdana menteri (ketika itu Najib), kata Americk Singh Sidhu, peguam kepada P Balasubramaniam, seorang penyiasat persendirian yang diupah oleh Razak untuk memantau pergerakan Altantuya.
"Saya tertanya-tanya mengapa dan untuk tujuan apa. Musa mengatur Azilah dan Sirul untuk Razak, tetapi mengapa melibatkan timbalan perdana menteri?"

Beliau percaya fail pasukan petugas khas yang ditubuhkan Thomas semasa pentadbiran Pakatan Harapan pada 2018–2020 patut dibuka semula, memandangkan temu bual dengan 40 saksi telah dijalankan berkaitan akuan berkanun Sirul pada 2019.

"Saya fikir ini adalah kes di mana kebenaran mesti dijelmakan. Kebenaran adalah mangsa dalam hal ini. Jelas sekali terdapat kepentingan tertentu, kuasa yang kuat. Atas apa jua sebab, mereka tidak mahu kebenaran dijelmakan, jadi mesti ada tekanan awam."

Bapa Altantuya, Shaariibuu Setev, seorang profesor dari Mongolia, terbang ke Malaysia lebih daripada 20 kali untuk menuntut keadilan bagi anaknya, dan berikrar tidak akan henti berusaha mencari lelaki yang mengarahkan anggota polis terbabit membunuhnya.
Pada Jun, perdana menteri baharu Mongolia, Nyam-Osoryn Uchral, memperakui kesengsaraan dan kesusahan kewangan yang ditanggung Shaariibuu dan mengurniakan sebuah pangsapuri kepadanya.
Dokumentari penuh boleh ditonton di pautan ini.

8e7ff175779f4d30: VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo XIV will leave the Rome hospital Saturday where he has been recovering from lung cancer surgery, the Vatican said, after doctors deemed him "fit for discharge".
Leo, 71, has been at the Gemelli hospital north of the Vatican since Tuesday, where doctors removed part of his right lung to extract a cancerous tumour.

"Considering the blood tests, the chest X-ray done this morning, and evaluating the clinical picture, the Holy Father has been deemed fit for discharge," wrote doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora in a note published by the Vatican.
The Vatican confirmed that "Pope Leo XIV will be discharged today from the Gemelli Polyclinic".
"He will leave the hospital in the early afternoon and return to the Vatican. Tomorrow he will recite the Angelus prayer from the window of the papal apartment," the Vatican said.

The Angelus prayer is typically given by the pope from the window of the Apostolic Palace, but in past years, former popes John Paul II and Francis similarly hospitalised at the Gemelli have delivered the prayer from the window of their hospital rooms.

9e2d43caca368c47: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The latest Street Fighter movie is bringing the arcade classic back to the big screen with flashy fights, larger-than-life characters and plenty of 1990s nostalgia — but Malaysian fans are finding that its storytelling doesn’t always land as well as its punches.

Directed by Kitao Sakurai and produced by Legendary Pictures and Capcom, the live-action adaptation opened in Malaysian cinemas on October 15, more than three decades after the franchise’s first big-screen outing.

Set in 1993, the film follows estranged fighters Ryu (Andrew Koji) and Ken Masters (Noah Centineo), who are drawn into the World Warrior Tournament by Chun-Li (Callina Liang), only to find themselves caught up in a conspiracy that forces them to confront each other and their past.
The ensemble cast also includes Jason Momoa as Blanka, Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson as Balrog, Joe “Roman Reigns” Anoa’i as Akuma and David Dastmalchian as M. Bison.
Previous adaptations, including the 1994 film starring Jean-Claude Van Damme and Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li (2009), received mixed reactions from fans and critics.
This time, however, the filmmakers have gone all in on the games’ colourful characters, exaggerated fighting moves and unapologetically campy humour.

And while reactions remain mixed, Malaysian fans who spoke to Malay Mail found plenty to enjoy in the film’s visual spectacle, familiar faces and nostalgic references — even if its plot left something to be desired.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Noah Centineo as Ken Masters in a scene inspired by the iconic car-smashing bonus stage from the ‘Street Fighter’ video games. — Picture courtesy of UIP International
Nostalgia hits hard, but the story takes a beating
For 29-year-old cosplayer and office clerk Alynn Lau, the film’s biggest strengths were its character portrayals, visual effects and 2D animated sequences.
However, she felt the plot was scattered and lacked a clear flow.
While Chun-Li remains one of her favourite characters, Alynn said Dhalsim stood out for his distinctive movements, which she felt stayed faithful to the game.

“If you grew up playing the game, this is definitely worth a watch! It brings back so many nostalgic memories, and seeing your favourite characters come to life on screen is always such an amazing experience,” she told Malay Mail.
Alynn would also welcome a sequel or spin-off that explores the characters and their stories further.
The film’s brief animated sequences left her particularly interested in seeing a full 2D animated adaptation.
Maya, 29, who works in human resources, was less enthusiastic.

Although the film fell short of her expectations as a fan, she still considered it the best Street Fighter adaptation to date, praising its visuals and encouraging fellow fans to keep an eye out for Easter eggs and references to the games.
Her favourite characters?
“E. Honda and Dhalsim! They were really great and fun to watch.
“It was just unfortunate that we didn’t get to see Dhalsim’s ‘Yoga Flame’,” she said.
For 37-year-old freelance prop maker Momo, who preferred to be identified only by that name, the film was a throwback to growing up in the 1990s, particularly through its music and humour.
Momo felt the film could appeal even to viewers unfamiliar with the games, while longtime fans would appreciate seeing familiar characters brought to life.
There was also enthusiasm for a possible sequel, with Momo hoping the filmmakers would expand on certain scenes and storylines, particularly following the film’s ending.
View this post on Instagram
A post shared by UIP Malaysia (@uipmalaysia)
Why going full camp might be the right move

Adapting Street Fighter has always presented filmmakers with a particular challenge: how do you build a coherent story around a fighting game whose biggest attractions are its outrageous characters and gravity-defying moves?
Sakurai’s answer appears to be simple: embrace the absurdity.
And for some critics, that approach is precisely what makes the new film entertaining.
Liz Shannon Miller, writing for Consequence, described the film at its best as a “deranged live-action cartoon”, adding that this was exactly what she wanted from the adaptation.
Time Out’s review highlighted its “hypersaturated neon colours and a sense of silliness”, which help turn the tournament setting into an entertaining, if somewhat exhausting, spectacle.
It’s an approach that makes sense for a franchise built around some of gaming’s most recognisable — and unlikely — fighters.
Blanka’s green skin and wild hair, Dhalsim’s stretchy limbs and yoga-inspired attacks, and the fireballs unleashed by Ryu and Ken are hardly suited to gritty realism.
Trying to make them more believable could strip away much of what makes them memorable.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Jason Momoa takes on the role of Blanka, the green-skinned fighter known for his wild hair and electrifying attacks, in the 2026 live-action adaptation of ‘Street Fighter’. — Picture courtesy of UIP International
Instead, the film leans into their fantastical abilities through stylised fight choreography, bold visual effects and familiar special moves.
Sakurai has said in previous interviews that he wanted to recapture the feeling of playing Street Fighter II in the 1990s, drawing inspiration from the era’s films, music and popular culture.
The result is a retro aesthetic that recreates the larger-than-life atmosphere of the arcade era that helped make Street Fighter a cultural phenomenon.
That nostalgia, however, has not been enough to convince everyone.

As of October 17, the film holds a 45 per cent critics’ score on Rotten Tomatoes, compared with an 84 per cent verified audience score — suggesting moviegoers are enjoying its chaotic spectacle more than critics.

For longtime fans, the film offers the thrill of seeing familiar fighters, signature moves and gaming references on the big screen. For newcomers, the tournament setting provides an introduction to a franchise that has spent nearly four decades establishing itself in gaming and popular culture.
The latest adaptation may not win over everyone, but the reactions from Malaysian fans suggest that Street Fighter doesn’t necessarily need a flawless plot to deliver an entertaining nostalgia trip.
Sometimes, the familiar faces, outrageous moves and sheer spectacle are enough to keep fans in the fight.
Street Fighter is now showing in Malaysian cinemas, including IMAX screenings.
b184cfbb3e1b5a7b: KOTA BARU: A Myanmar man believed to be acting as a transporter was arrested with 10 fellow citizens during an Immigration Department raid at a hotel in Wakaf Che Yeh.
Immigration Department deputy director-general (Operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said the group comprised six men and four women who were believed to be working in Johor Baru and Kuala Lumpur.
He said they arrived in Kelantan at about 6.30am and checked into the hotel, which was believed to be a temporary transit point.
At 8.30am, the Kelantan Immigration Department raided the hotel and foiled an attempt to take all 10 undocumented migrants out of the country through an illegal route for their return to Myanmar.
Officers also found a Honda CR-V sport utility vehicle believed to have been used to transport the migrants, along with several bags belonging to them.
Preliminary investigations found that each Myanmar citizen was required to pay the transporter RM3,500 to be taken out of the country.
Lokman Effendi said the transporter, who was in his 30s, admitted to having lived in Shah Alam, Selangor, for four years.
All 11 were detained to assist investigations under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.

In a separate operation at a construction site in Kubang Kerian, the Kelantan Immigration Department inspected 57 foreign workers and detained 55 on suspicion of various immigration offences, Lokman Effendi said.
From Jan 1 to Oct 15, the department conducted 11,000 enforcement operations nationwide, during which more than 146,000 foreign workers were inspected.
More than 65,000 people were detained for various immigration offences, while more than 45,000 foreign workers were repatriated to their countries of origin.
Lokman Effendisaid the 11,000 operations carried out over 287 days amounted to an average of about 38 operations a day.
On average, about 511 foreign workers were inspected daily, while 228 people were detained for various immigration offences.
da78431c8b1faec0: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian model Vibha Rajish nearly skipped an audition for what she believed was an ordinary sportswear commercial, unaware that the opportunity would place her on set with Hollywood star Zendaya.
The 23-year-old eventually landed a role in "Zendaya in Your New Favourite Action Movie", a two-minute campaign film for Swiss sportswear brand On.
Released on YouTube on 1 Oct, the cinematic advertisement features Zendaya in a showdown with female martial artists, with Vibha appearing briefly as one of the fighters pursuing the actress.
Vibha initially considered missing the audition because she had a wedding to attend in Belgium.
When she decided to go ahead, she thought the job would provide extra pocket money for her summer holidays.
She learnt she had been selected just two days before filming and was asked to return for the shoot.
The casting call had made no mention of Zendaya, referring only to a "sportswear ad".
Vibha discovered the identity of the leading star only after arriving for rehearsals and noticing two unusually large trailers.
"Initially there was no mention of Z (as we called her on set)," she said in a news report.
After meeting other women who had been training for the shoot, she realised something big was happening.
They eventually explained that the trailer marked "Z" belonged to Zendaya, while the other was for the actress's celebrated stylist, Law Roach, whom Vibha admired.

"It was so surreal that this little girl from Bandar Utama was about to meet, let alone act alongside Zendaya in her prime," she said, describing the experience as emotional, gratifying and a source of pride.
Despite the hectic filming schedule, Vibha found Zendaya warm and considerate towards the people around her.
The actress even offered her pizza, although Vibha was too nervous to accept.
"It was a very hectic few days but yes! She was lovely to everyone; she even offered me pizza. No, I didn't take it cos I was too nervous and freaked out lol," she said.

Born in Kuala Lumpur and raised in Petaling Jaya, Vibha described her upbringing as typically Malaysian, with her kindergarten, primary and secondary schools all within about two kilometres of her family home.
Her modelling journey began at 16, when she wanted to help pay for treatment for her cat, MJ, which had been diagnosed with feline immunodeficiency virus.

With retail jobs difficult to secure during the Covid-19 pandemic, she teamed up with a neighbourhood friend who was an aspiring photographer, exchanging modelling photographs for his experience behind the camera.
"That's where it all began!" she recalled.
Her journey later took her to Prague, a city she had first encountered in a fantasy book and was drawn to partly because of its comparatively affordable living costs.
During her first year there, a modelling scout approached her, leading to an agency contract.
She initially balanced her studies, modelling assignments and part-time work, but the industry has since become her main source of income.
After five years abroad, she hopes to explore acting opportunities in Malaysia, particularly in Bahasa Malaysia.
"I would love to do some acting in Malaysia and in Bahasa specifically," she said.

"My Malay has deteriorated a little since living abroad for five years, but I love a challenge and it would be so special to me to do something local. I'll be back in January so I'm just excited to be back home, eat good food and see what Malaysia has in store for me."

d8c10baec9f8ca6f: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 17 — Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor is scheduled to address more than 3,000 delegates and observers at the 2026 GRS Convention in Kudat tomorrow (Sunday), which aims to prepare the coalition to win at least 16 of the 26 parliamentary seats.

“Although GRS was returned to power in the State election in November last year, the convention also serves to remind that GRS should not rest on its laurels but continue to work hard towards the betterment of the State and people.

“Cooperation and unity among GRS components as well as our partners in the State Unity Government is vital to ensure a decisive victory for GRS in the coming general election,” said Hajiji, who is GRS Chairman and PGRS President.

The inaugural convention in Kudat will be held at Dewan Tun Mustapha, with participants and observers representing all 26 parliamentary constituencies in Sabah, including Labuan.Hajiji said the venue follows a decision by the GRS Supreme Council that the convention should be rotated among the various districts instead of being centred solely in Kota Kinabalu.
Besides Hajiji’s keynote address, the six GRS Deputy Chairmen will deliver speeches. They represent the core leadership of the six GRS component parties, namely PGRS, PBS, PCS, LDP, PHRS and Upko.
Hajiji said the convention will bring together central leadership and key divisional leaders for discussions and sharing sessions with two focuses.
The first is political strategy to strengthen party preparedness, particularly ahead of the 16th General Election.
The second is an assessment of progress on the development agenda for the people and the State under the GRS Manifesto, specifically by advancing the Hala Tuju Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) 2.0 roadmap.
He said GRS’ partners in the State Government are also expected to perform well and deliver more seats so that Sabah’s voice can be heard in Parliament.
Hajiji added that the political dynamics in Sabah favour GRS and the coalition will enter the general election with full confidence of gaining the trust of voters.

The choice of Kudat is seen by many as a sign of GRS’ confidence in capturing the Kota Marudu and Kudat parliamentary seats, which are held by Parti KDM and an Independent respectively. Both Members of Parliament lost in the State election in November last year to GRS candidates.­ — Daily Express

* Editor’s note: GRS stands for Gabungan Rakyat Sabah; PGRS stands for Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah; PBS stands for Parti Bersatu Sabah; PCS stands for Parti Cinta Sabah; LDP stands for Liberal Democratic Party; PHRS stands for Parti Harapan Rakyat Sabah; Upko stands for United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation; and SMJ stands for Sabah Maju Jaya.
b92a7cb36fc5e436: KUCHING: The next Sarawak state election is likely to be held in December, says Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) information chief Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah.

Karim, who is also the state tourism, creative industry and performing arts minister, said premier Abang Johari Openg had yet to announce when the state assembly would be dissolved, noting that December would mark five years since the last state election on Dec 18, 2021.
Under the law, a state election must be held within 60 days of the dissolution of the state assembly. The state assembly’s term ends in February.
“Even if he (Abang Johari) calls it at the end of this month or in November, the election has to be held in December.
“December is usually the year-end period, and with Christmas, people take leave, so it has to be around that time,” he told a press conference after a writing competition award ceremony here today.
Karim said the window for holding the election was narrowing and the Election Commission would need to consider the festive calendar when setting the polling date.
He said Chinese New Year falls in January, followed by Ramadan in February, making either month unsuitable for the polls.
Karim was previously reported as saying that the state assembly was expected to be dissolved in November, or two weeks after the state’s 2027 budget is passed.
a3ba5e433ed143ad: COLOMBO: Sri Lanka suffered a nationwide electricity blackout on Saturday after the national grid tripped, possibly because solar power generation exceeded consumption, officials said.
The country was without grid power for more than two hours, with no clear timeline for when electricity would be restored.
State-run Electricity Distribution Lanka (EDL) said engineers were working to fix a fault affecting the entire grid and suspected excess solar power had caused the breakdown.
Energy Minister Anura Karunathilaka said authorities hoped to restore supplies "stage by stage".
"We request rooftop solar system owners to disconnect their systems until further instructions in order to support the restoration efforts," he said in a brief statement.
The entire grid shut down in February 2025, when solar power generation exceeded consumption on a bright, sunny Sunday. It took more than six hours to restore supplies.
Sri Lanka has an installed solar power capacity of just over 3,000 megawatts, while daytime demand ranges from 2,000 to 2,500 megawatts.

721bb044e267fa63: KUCHING, Oct 17 — Sarawak could hold its 13th state election as early as November, with the polling window extending to mid-December, said State Tourism, Creative Industry and Performing Arts Minister Dato Sri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah.
“The window is getting smaller. I would say we only have about one and a half months — November and half of December,” he told reporters at an event here.

Abdul Karim, who is also Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) information chief, said the timing would depend on when Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg dissolves the Sarawak Legislative Assembly.
The Election Commission (EC) would then determine the polling date in accordance with the law, he said.
He added that the election timetable must allow sufficient time for the EC to prepare and for campaigning to take place.
A state election must be held within 60 days of the Assembly’s dissolution, a deadline that also applies if its term expires automatically. — Borneo Post
* Editor’s note: The abbreviation DUN in Malay stands for Dewan Undangan Negeri, or State Legislative Assembly.
9ebc04462b4e9359: ROME, Oct 17 — Pope Leo XIV will leave the Rome hospital today where he has been recovering from lung cancer surgery, the Vatican said, after doctors deemed him “fit for discharge”.
Leo, 71, has been at the Gemelli hospital north of the Vatican since Tuesday, where doctors removed part of his right lung to extract a cancerous tumour.

“Considering the blood tests, the chest X-ray done this morning, and evaluating the clinical picture, the Holy Father has been deemed fit for discharge,” doctors Luigi Carbone and Stefano Margaritora wrote in a note published by the Vatican.
The Vatican confirmed that “Pope Leo XIV will be discharged today”.
“He will leave the hospital in the early afternoon and return to the Vatican. Tomorrow he will recite the Angelus prayer from the window of the papal apartment,” the Vatican said.
The Angelus prayer is typically given by the pope from the window of the Apostolic Palace overlooking St Peter’s Square.
But in past years, former popes John Paul II and Francis similarly hospitalised at the Gemelli have delivered the prayer from the window of their hospital rooms.
The Vatican’s press office said that Leo celebrated mass today, as he has in recent days, in a room on the 10th floor of the hospital where he has been recovering.
News that the otherwise healthy and sporty pope had a cancerous tumour removed from his lung has rattled the Vatican and the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics.
But his doctors have said Leo’s recovery has been progressing normally as they await the results of tests that will determine the course of action to take.
Leo has resumed some work, making a call on Friday to Russian President Vladimir Putin to urge a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky.
Up in the air, however, is a planned papal voyage to South America, scheduled for November 6-17 to visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.
Pope watchers say that Leo — who spent two decades as a missionary in Peru — is anxious to make the long journey, but will likely follow the recommendations of his doctors.
Leo has cancelled all his audiences until October 20.

The pope himself announced to the public in St Peter’s Square last Sunday, following the Angelus prayer, that a routine medical examination had revealed a nodule that doctors recommended should be removed. — AFP
f30538a405eda442: KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 25 air quality monitoring stations nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, with Pasir Gudang in Johor recording the highest at 198.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System, Negri Sembilan's Nilai and Seremban recorded readings of 180 and 176 respectively.
In Johor, Larkin recorded an API reading of 175, followed by Pengerang (174), Kota Tinggi (173), Batu Pahat (171), Tangkak (167), Segamat (161) and Kluang (161).
In Selangor, Shah Alam and Johan Setia recorded readings of 172 each, followed by Klang (171), Petaling Jaya (169), Banting (160) and Kuala Selangor (109).
In Melaka, Alor Gajah and Bukit Rambai recorded readings of 168 each, while Bandaraya Melaka recorded 162.
Putrajaya recorded an API reading of 166, while Cheras and Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded 164 and 163 respectively.
In Sabah, Sandakan recorded a reading of 157, while Tawau recorded 129.
Another 42 monitoring stations recorded moderate air quality.
These included Seri Manjung in Perak, with an API reading of 96, followed by Tanjung Malim (91), Pegoh in Ipoh (89) and Tasek in Ipoh (88).
In Sarawak, the Serian police headquarters monitoring station recorded a reading of 82, followed by Sri Aman (80) and Samarahan (79).
In Pahang, Rompin recorded an API reading of 78, followed by Temerloh (76) and Indera Mahkota in Kuantan (75).
Limbang in Sarawak was the only monitoring station to record good air quality, with an API reading of 50.
ce780537dec8fb5e: CYBERJAYA: Pas has prepared a list of potential candidates for the upcoming Melaka election, with the final selection to be decided by the party's central leadership.
Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang said the list contained numerous names for consideration.
"There are many candidates on the list. Deciding who will ultimately contest is up to the Pas central leadership," he told a press conference after launching the Tafsir Al-Tibyan book here today.
He was responding to questions about Pas' candidates after Barisan Nasional confirmed that its candidate list was complete.
Yesterday, Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the coalition's list was ready and could be announced at any time.
Rauf was reported to have said he would not take long to announce the candidates as nomination day was approaching.
On the number of seats Pas would contest in the Melaka election, Hadi, who is also the Marang member of parliament, said discussions were still ongoing.
"The number of seats is still under discussion. The matter is still being discussed.
"It will be announced closer to nomination day," he said.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka election, with nomination day on Oct 31 and early voting on Nov 10.
Melaka has 28 state seats. BN won 21 in the previous election, while Pakatan Harapan won five and Perikatan Nasional secured two.
3c6a059e296e2bfb: MADRID: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said Saturday if he were winger Vinicius Junior, he would have left the club this summer.
The Brazilian was sent off during Madrid's win over Villarreal last weekend for hair pulling and was banned for four matches, meaning he will miss the Clasico clash against Barcelona on Oct 25.
Vinicius, 26, has also been targeted regularly by opposition fans and been racially abused on many occasions since joining Madrid in 2018.
"He's a spectacular kid who it's easy to have a good relationship with," Mourinho told reporters.
"He's a fantastic boy, tremendous credit to him for the fact that he keeps living and surviving and still having a smile...
"If it were me in his place, probably I wouldn't be here. In this last summer I would have forced an exit to a league, a country, or somewhere there are rival clubs and stadiums that respect him."
In the summer, Vinicius signed a new contract with Real Madrid until 2032.
Question marks remain over whether Madrid can line up with attacking superstars Vinicius, Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham together, without losing balance.
"Because he loves Real Madrid, for loving the club and the city, and for believing that things can always improve, he renewed, and he keeps on smiling," continued Mourinho.
"No one or nobody can... well, influence him negatively, yes, because he's human... but take away his joy of living and working and being with his teammates, no, no one can do that."

Mourinho took Vinicius off during the 4-3 Champions League win at Roma on Wednesday, with the winger still struggling to return to the form that helped him win the competition twice under Carlo Ancelotti.
Mourinho said he was happy that Vinicius's ban was four matches, saying he thought some hidden figures at the Spanish football federation's disciplinary committee "would give him one or two more".
'There are limits'
Madrid face Sevilla on Sunday aiming not to fall further behind league leaders Barcelona, who visit Real Betis later on Saturday.
Hansi Flick's Barcelona have won every single match this season and are six points ahead of fourth-placed Real Madrid.
Los Blancos and Mourinho have blamed referees for some of their results, including the 2-1 derby defeat by Atletico Madrid in September.
On Friday Real Madrid called for La Liga president Javier Tebas to resign after he compared the club's efforts to discredit referees to the techniques of Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels.
Tebas later attempted to clarify that he was drawing comparisons with "those propaganda techniques" and not with the ideology of the Nazis.
"I don't want to talk about this, there are limits, and there are limits. You can only excuse it if it's a clinical case – otherwise there's no excuse," said Mourinho.
"I don't want to go down that road. Madrid and its fans understand what it is up against.
"For the prestige that the league has abroad, for being the current world champions, it's better if we try to keep this here and not let it get out (to the world)."
