d9ad1ab514e787dd: From P Kamalanathan
Last week, a young student at AIMST University asked me: “Datuk, did Rajinikanth go to university?”
I smiled.
Rajini studied in a Kannada-medium school and worked as a coolie, carpenter and bus conductor in Bangalore.
He joined a film institute at 25, an age when we tell our youth, “You are late.”
Last week, Jailer 2 was breaking box-office records again. At 74, he is still a superstar.
We celebrate his punchlines, but we ignore his lessons on education.
As a former deputy minister of education who oversaw five million students, I see five lessons from Rajini that our new National Education Plan 2026-2035 is trying to teach.
First: Learning agility beats certificates
Rajini had no degree. But he had what the ministry now calls “learning agility”. From stage plays to learning Hindi for Andha Kanoon to learning motion capture for Enthiran, he never stopped.
In Switzerland this year, I saw Swiss CEOs with no MBAs but 10 micro-credentials in AI. That is the Rajini model: lifelong TVET.
Second: Discipline is education
Director SP Muthuraman once said that Rajini was the first to arrive and the last to leave. In 50 years, there has been no “Rajini late” headline.
We chase tuition, but our students fail because they cannot wake up at 6am. Discipline, like that of the Bangalore bus conductor punching tickets at 5am, is the first certificate.
Third: Humility is Karamah Insaniah
The National Education Plan speaks of Karamah Insaniah, or the recognition and uplifting of human dignity. Look at Rajini.
He is a superstar, yet he sits on the floor, touches elders' feet and says, “I am a small child of K Balachander.”
In an age of TikTok arrogance, he teaches adab. My mother always taught me that education without humility is noise.
Fourth: Reinvention in the AI age

Rajini, at 74, is learning AI filmmaking for Jailer 2. If a 74-year-old can act with de-ageing technology, our youth can earn Google AI certification, which the United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) offers free in Selangor.
Fifth: Do well, do good

Rajini famously said, “Money comes, goes. Give.” He built schools quietly. This is what I tell my colleagues at the Public Relations Practitioners Society of Malaysia: sustainability is a competitive advantage. Rajini has sustained a 50-year career because people trust his goodness.
That student asked if Rajini passed his exams. I told him: He did not pass with straight As, but he passed the hardest exam: life.
This Deepavali, when we watch Rajini on screen, let us tell our children:
Don’t copy his style; copy his discipline.
Don’t just whistle for the superstar; learn to be a superstar in your own trade, whether as a welder, coder or teacher.
Because, as Rajini said in Padayappa: “En vazhi, thani vazhi”, or “My way is my own way”.
Let our education system allow every Malaysian child to find their own way.
P Kamalanathan is an MIC central working committee member and a former deputy education minister.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
285e03e2db9707e0: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to firm up its direction for the Melaka state election within a week, with candidate selection now in its final stages, coalition election strategy director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said today.

He said the coalition wanted to field candidates with a record of serving the community and relevant experience, while giving newcomers opportunities in some constituencies where its traditional support was weaker.

“In some state constituencies where our support is relatively low, we will allow candidates to gain experience. This is part of the party’s and Pakatan Harapan’s long-term plan,” he told reporters after attending the Semarak Kasih event with Yayasan Selangor students here, national news wire Bernama reported.
Amirudin said allowing candidates to gain experience in less favourable constituencies could help build a longer-term plan for PKR and the wider coalition.
He also touched on possible cooperation with Bersatu, saying the matter had not been finalised and a decision would be made soon.
PKR has previously confirmed that it will contest nine seats in the Melaka election.
Party secretary-general Datuk Fuziah Salleh said Pakatan Harapan would contest more seats overall if PKR’s allocation remained at nine.
PH is scheduled to announce its candidate on October 24.
The Melaka state election has been set for November 14 with nominations on October 31 and early voting on November 10.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional won 21 of the 28 seats, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional two.
db37c052738f24c1: KUALA LUMPUR: Motorists plying Jalan Maarof in Bangsar are calling on authorities to address severe daily traffic gridlocks affecting commutes into the commercial hub.
Drivers said the stretch turns into a persistent bottleneck during peak hours, driven by heavy traffic merging from multiple directions into narrow two-lane roads.
Personal driver Muhammad Naim, 35, said the area experiences congestion during morning, noon, and evening rush hours.

"Traffic comes in from three different directions, including Pantai and Brickfields, alongside cars making U-turns. Everything squeezes into just two narrow lanes, so a bottleneck is bound to happen," he told the New Straits Times.
Naim added that indiscriminate roadside parking exacerbates the congestion.
"The road is just too narrow for so many cars. It only has two lanes handling heavy traffic, and when cars are parked along the roadside, it makes it even harder to move through.

"This has been going on for years. It's a main road leading to Bangsar Shopping Centre and Damansara, making it one of the worst traffic spots around here," he said, proposing that traffic wardens be stationed to direct merging traffic.
Grab driver Zarif Fadli, 25, said peak-hour congestion extends from Jalan Bangsar all the way up to Jalan Maarof.
"Whether it is the morning rush, the evening commute, or the stretch heading towards Mid Valley, drivers are constantly stuck in traffic.

"The jam from Jalan Bangsar is bad in the morning and evening, especially during peak hours. Double parking along the road makes it much worse. We need better public transport services so people don't have to drive into Bangsar every day," he said.
Food delivery rider Pankaj Kumar, 56, a 25-year resident, said gridlock across Bangsar and neighbouring Brickfields has turned daily travel into a hassle.
"Driving around Bangsar and Brickfields is absolute torture. The gridlock is unavoidable during morning and evening rush hours, but it now happens even on weekends and rainy days.

"The issue is indiscriminate parking and rampant double parking. People park illegally and claim it is 'just for five minutes', but then leave their cars for half an hour or two hours," he said, urging Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) to step up patrols and enforcement.
Bukit Bandaraya Residents Association adviser Datuk M. Ali said traffic enforcement in the city has largely collapsed, leading to widespread double parking and severe bottlenecks.

"Strict, consistent, and persistent enforcement without compromise is urgently needed to tackle the worsening traffic congestion. People must be made to be disciplined and accountable. If they are not adhering to persuasion, then go in and use a hard stick instead of a carrot," he said.

Ali noted that while authorities occasionally issue summonses following public complaints, DBKL should leverage surveillance cameras across the capital to monitor traffic and conduct random towing of illegally parked vehicles.
The New Straits Times has reached out to DBKL for comment.
25b044a912e8ccdf: MELAKA, Oct 17 — Sarawak could strengthen the country’s cocoa industry by expanding cultivation areas and producing higher-value chocolate products, helping narrow the supply gap in dried cocoa beans, which currently relies heavily on imports, over the next two to three years.

Malaysian Cocoa Board acting director-general Shari Fuddin Sha’ari said expanding cocoa cultivation in Sarawak, alongside Sabah, the country’s main cocoa-producing state, could increase local raw material supplies once newly planted trees begin bearing fruit.

He said the industry’s expansion should also be matched by stronger downstream activities so farmers don’t have to rely solely on selling dried cocoa beans and can process them into higher-value chocolate products.
“We see considerable potential throughout the cocoa industry value chain.

“Dried cocoa beans can be turned into chocolate products, and we can bring the processing technology to interested farmers and entrepreneurs,” he told reporters at the launch of ‘A Malaysian Cocoa Affair 2026’ event here today, officiated by Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Noraini Ahmad.

Shari Fuddin said the Malaysian Cocoa Board was also pioneering chocolate production using Sarawak cocoa beans through a single-origin approach, with dried beans from four locations processed at a cluster cooperative research centre in Kota Samarahan.

“Cocoa beans from different locations have distinct flavour and aroma profiles influenced by factors such as growing areas and processing methods, creating opportunities to produce chocolates with their own unique identities.
“These characteristics can be used by entrepreneurs to develop various chocolate formulations, including blends of local cocoa beans with ingredients such as gula Melaka,” he said.
He said the approach could also attract more entrepreneurs, particularly young people, to the cocoa industry by focusing on innovation, product development and marketing.
Shari Fuddin said farmers remained interested in cocoa cultivation, with some applying for assistance to start or expand their plantations.
He added that allocations under the latest Malaysia Plan (MP) also supported efforts to expand cocoa-growing areas, providing further opportunities for the industry to grow.

“We hope increased local production will help narrow the supply gap for dried cocoa beans from overseas. This will also create greater economic opportunities for farmers and entrepreneurs through the production of downstream products,” he said. — Bernama
8f2f8b442271dc2e: COLOMBO, Oct 17 — Sri Lanka suffered a nationwide electricity blackout today after the national grid tripped, possibly because solar power generation exceeded consumption, officials said.
The country was without grid power for more than two hours, with no clear timeline for when electricity would be restored.
State-run Electricity Distribution Lanka (EDL) said engineers were working to fix a fault affecting the entire grid, and suspected excess solar power had caused the breakdown.
Energy Minister Anura Karunathilaka said authorities hoped to restore supplies “stage by stage”.
“We request rooftop solar system owners to disconnect their systems until further instructions in order to support the restoration efforts,” he said in a brief statement.
The entire grid shut down in February 2025, when solar power generation exceeded consumption on a bright, sunny Sunday. It took more than six hours to restore supplies.
Sri Lanka has an installed solar power capacity of just over 3,000 megawatts, while daytime demand ranges from 2,000 to 2,500 megawatts.
Tax concessions have encouraged consumers to switch to solar and sell their surplus electricity to the grid, creating imbalances that the utility provider is struggling to manage.
The government aims to increase solar power generation capacity to nearly 4,400 megawatts within three years — a 388 per cent increase from 2024. — AFP
c31584e89bf0b873: PUTRAJAYA: Sebanyak 6,724 pegawai Kementerian Kesihatan (KKM) daripada pelbagai skim perkhidmatan diluluskan pemangkuan dan kenaikan pangkat ke Jawatan Utama Sektor Awam (JUSA) serta gred 10 hingga gred 15 oleh Lembaga Kenaikan Pangkat Perkhidmatan Awam (LKPPA) pada 13 Okt lepas.

KKM dalam kenyataan berkata kelulusan itu merupakan sebahagian daripada usaha berterusan kementerian untuk menghargai komitmen, dedikasi dan pencapaian pegawai dalam memastikan kelancaran operasi serta keberkesanan penyampaian perkhidmatan kesihatan kepada rakyat.

"Selaras dengan penambahbaikan laluan kemajuan kerjaya di bawah Sistem Saraan Perkhidmatan Awam (SSPA), LKPPA meluluskan Kriteria Kecemerlangan Kenaikan Pangkat Tanpa Kekosongan Jawatan Bagi Skim Perkhidmatan Pengajar KKM.
"Kelulusan ini memberi peluang kepada pegawai terlibat menikmati laluan kemajuan kerjaya yang lebih baik," kata KKM.

Selain itu, KKM turut merakamkan penghargaan atas jasa dan pengorbanan empat pegawai KKM yang berkhidmat sebagai anggota Perkhidmatan Doktor Udara (PDU) dan maut dalam nahas helikopter ketika menjalankan tugas pada 8 Sept lepas.
Sebagai tanda penghargaan atas jasa dan khidmat bakti yang telah dicurahkan, keempat-empat pegawai tersebut diluluskan kenaikan pangkat secara anumerta (posthumous).

"KKM percaya bahawa pengiktirafan seperti ini akan menjadi pemangkin kepada kecemerlangan berterusan serta memperkukuh semangat pegawai KKM untuk bersama-sama merealisasikan aspirasi sistem kesihatan negara yang berkualiti, mampan dan responsif," menurut KKM.
KKM juga akan terus meneliti dan melaksanakan langkah penambahbaikan dari semasa ke semasa bagi memastikan kebajikan serta pembangunan kerjaya pegawai KKM sentiasa diberi perhatian sewajarnya.
0f5b01e8b9023008: KUALA LUMPUR: Men's doubles pair Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik put their strength in serve and return to good use to secure a place in the Denmark Open final on Saturday.
The world No. 4 defeated South Korea's world No. 1 Kim Won Ho-Seo Seung Jae 21-14, 21-18 in the semi-finals at the SJF Bank Arena.
Aaron said their ability to take charge of the opening exchanges was an advantage they needed to keep exploiting.
"Serving and receiving are our strong points as a pair, and we have to use that to our advantage at all times," said Aaron.
The victory also marked another encouraging turn in their rivalry with Won Ho–Seung Jae, after the Koreans defeated them in two three-game matches earlier this year.
The top-ranked Koreans had denied Aaron-Wooi Yik the Malaysian Open and All England titles earlier this year.
The Malaysians have now beaten them in straight games in successive meetings, having also prevailed at the World Championships.
Wooi Yik pointed to improvements in his back-court play and their continuing efforts to sharpen control and shuttle movement, particularly at crucial moments.
He said their decade-long understanding provided a strong foundation, with the focus now on refining the finer details of their game.
"Our partnership has been 10 years. Our combination is good. There are some details where we need to try different things," said Wooi Yik.
Their run to the final has also encouraged them in their first tournament back together after a temporary split.
Aaron said they had rediscovered their enjoyment on court and were playing with less pressure.
"We've been enjoying ourselves more on court. Maybe the pressure is not too much now for us," he said.
Wooi Yik described their return as "a positive sign for us to move forward", with the pair now one win away from the Denmark Open title.
They will face either Indonesia's Fajar Alfian-Shohibul Fikri or China's Liang Wei Keng-Wang Chang in the final.
aa337b964b1b6ab3: PUTRAJAYA: Four Health Ministry (MOH) officers who died in a helicopter crash while on duty on Sept 8 have been promoted posthumously in recognition of their service and dedication.
The ministry honoured the healthcare staff who served with the Flying Doctor Service (PDU), whose promotions were approved by the Public Service Promotion Board (LKPPA) on Oct 13.

The board cleared 6,724 officers from various service schemes under the ministry for acting appointments and promotions to the Senior Management Service (JUSA) and Grades 10 to 15, the ministry said in a statement.
The approvals reflect the ministry's continued efforts to recognise officers' commitment, dedication and achievements in ensuring smooth operations and effective healthcare service delivery.

In line with improvements to career progression under the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), the board also approved excellence-based promotion criteria for officers under the ministry's teaching service scheme, allowing them to be promoted without a vacant post.
The approval provides the officers concerned with better opportunities for career advancement.

The ministry expressed confidence that such recognition would encourage continued excellence and strengthen officers' commitment to building a high-quality, sustainable and responsive national healthcare system.
It said it would continue to review and implement improvements to ensure officers' welfare and career development received due attention.
b04cc0882aa4578e: MACHANG, Oct 17 — Police are maintaining round-the-clock surveillance along all border routes in Kelantan to curb cross-border crime, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said the directive had been issued to Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat to ensure continuous physical surveillance along the border.

“Among the measures taken are the demolition of illegal jetties and enforcement of the law against individuals crossing the border without valid documents,” he told a press conference after attending the launch ceremony for the 2026 Home Ministry’s Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani initiatives here today.
However, he said enforcement measures might not completely eliminate cross-border crime, as it involves organised criminal networks that had been operating for a long time.
Therefore, Saifuddin Nasution said efforts to curb such activities required the cooperation of all parties and could not rely solely on the Home Ministry and the police.

Meanwhile, when asked to comment on the case involving an incident concerning Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1, he said police were completing several aspects of the investigation papers after the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) requested improvements before a further decision could be made.
Saifuddin Nasution said the investigation papers had been submitted to the AGC within a week of the incident.
He said the AGC subsequently asked police to complete several aspects of the investigation to ensure that the information and evidence gathered were sufficient for further consideration.
He said the investigation papers included witness statements and information gathered throughout the investigation.
The AGC could return the investigation papers to police for further completion if additional information was required before a decision was made, he added.

Previously, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail was reported as saying that the investigation was being conducted by the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which deals with voluntarily causing hurt to another person.
Mohd Khalid said statements had been recorded from 25 witnesses so far to assist in the investigation into the incident, which occurred on September 28.

The media had earlier reported that Mohd Shuhaily had left it to the government to decide on any action that might be taken against him following a viral video showing him reprimanding an individual at KLIA Terminal 1.
Mohd Shuhaily said the matter had been brought to the attention of the country’s top leadership and the Home Ministry, and that he was prepared to accept any decision on the issue. — Bernama
a1ed37d5812218dd: TOKYO: Japan's weather agency withdrew an erroneous alert for a magnitude 9.9 earthquake minutes after issuing it, apologising for a warning that disrupted transport.

The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) had initially warned on Friday that a magnitude 9.9 earthquake had occurred near the Kuril Islands, known in Japan as the Chishima Islands, triggering loud emergency alerts on millions of mobile phones.
The JMA later clarified that a magnitude 6.9 quake had occurred near Russia's Kamchatka Peninsula at a depth of 160km just after midday.
"We deeply apologise for the significant inconvenience and concern caused to the public," JMA official Shinya Tsukada told reporters.
The alert did not cause widespread panic but briefly disrupted public transport.
According to the JMA, the error stemmed from an anomaly in calculating the earthquake's epicentre.
The estimated magnitude was based on an incorrect assumption that the epicentre was about 680 kilometres farther from Japan than it actually was, the weather agency said.
Japan is haunted by the memory of a massive magnitude 9.0 undersea quake in 2011, which triggered a tsunami that killed or left missing around 18,500 people and wrecked the Fukushima nuclear plant.
A magnitude 9.9 tremor would have released about 22 times as much energy as the 2011 quake, according to local media.
4e59ea21f998b38c: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 17 — A total of 6,724 officers from various service schemes under the Ministry of Health (MOH) have been approved for acting appointments and promotions to the Senior Management Service (JUSA) and Grades 10 to 15.
The approvals were granted by the Public Service Promotion Board (LKPPA) on October 13, according to a statement issued today.
The move reflects the ministry’s continued efforts to recognise officers’ commitment, dedication and achievements in ensuring smooth operations and effective healthcare service delivery.

In line with improvements to career progression under the Public Service Remuneration System (SSPA), the board also approved excellence-based promotion criteria for officers under MOH’s teaching service scheme, allowing them to be promoted without a vacant post.
The approval provides the officers concerned with better opportunities for career advancement.
The ministry also paid tribute to four officers who served with the Flying Doctor Service (PDU) and died in a helicopter crash while on duty on September 8.
All four were approved for posthumous promotions in recognition of their service and dedication.

The ministry expressed confidence that such recognition would encourage continued excellence and strengthen officers’ commitment to building a high-quality, sustainable and responsive national healthcare system.
It will continue to review and implement improvements to ensure officers’ welfare and career development receive due attention. — Bernama
0c8a8cd1e399ad9e: MACHANG: Four states — Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu — have recorded drug involvement rates above the national threshold, with Pendang in Kedah and Kuala Krai in Kelantan emerging as the country's two highest-ranking districts.

Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the figures were calculated based on the number of people involved in drug cases per 100,000 population, using an international standard adopted by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).
He said Tumpat, Tanah Merah and Bachok in Kelantan, as well as Besut in Terengganu, were also identified as critical districts, with rates exceeding 1,000 cases per 100,000 population.
"These are all concerns for us, and not just for one state.

"Besides Kelantan, three other states are also showing worrying figures and an increasing trend," he told reporters after the Home Ministry's Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani programmes at Sekolah Kebangsaan Jambu Lawar here today.

Saifuddin said drug abuse among children below 15 was also becoming increasingly worrying, while those aged between 15 and 39 remained the largest group involved in drug abuse based on available profiles.
He said the trend called for more comprehensive preventive measures, including early education and greater parental involvement, to prevent young people from becoming involved in drug abuse.
"The National Anti-Drug Agency (Nada) has three main functions — education and prevention, enforcement, and rehabilitation.
"We must strengthen public education to raise awareness and encourage families to take preventive action," he said.

On efforts to curb drug-related activities along the Kelantan-Thailand border, Saifuddin said he had directed the Kelantan police chief to ensure round-the-clock surveillance along all stretches of the border.
He said the strategy included maintaining a visible police presence, demolishing illegal jetties and enforcing the Immigration Act against undocumented cross-border movements.
However, he acknowledged that these measures could not completely eliminate the problem, as drug-related crime was linked to organised criminal networks that had been operating for decades.
"Our actions can help reduce the problem, but they cannot eliminate it entirely.
"This is the responsibility of the Home Ministry and the police, but it is not enough. It must be a shared responsibility," he said.
b4a01d74e85056ca: PETALING JAYA: Kementerian Perdagangan Dalam Negeri dan Kos Sara Hidup (KPDN) Selangor menerima 10 aduan rasmi mengenai petrol RON95 yang didakwa bercampur air sehingga menyebabkan kerosakan kenderaan pengguna di beberapa kawasan di negeri itu.
Pengarah KPDN Selangor Muhamad Hanif Asa’ari berkata susulan aduan itu pihaknya semalam menjalankan siasatan lapangan dan tindakan penguatkuasaan di tujuh premis stesen minyak.

“Hasil di lapangan, sebanyak 27 tin sampel petrol RON95 telah diambil dan disita daripada pam pengisian yang terjejas untuk dihantar ke Jabatan Kimia Malaysia bagi analisis makmal,” katanya dalam kenyataan lapor Bernama.
Beliau berkata pemeriksaan awal mendapati kesemua premis berkenaan memiliki Lesen Kebenaran Khas (CSA) dan lesen di bawah Akta Kemajuan Petroleum 1974 (PDA) yang masih sah.

Katanya, KPDN juga mengeluarkan notis di bawah Seksyen 32 Akta Perihal Dagangan 2011 bagi menghendaki pemilik stesen minyak mengemukakan maklumat dan dokumen berkaitan perniagaan untuk membantu siasatan.

“Siasatan dijalankan berhubung kemungkinan berlaku pelanggaran Seksyen 5(1)(c), dibaca bersama Seksyen 6(1)(d) dan Seksyen 7 Akta Perihal Dagangan 2011, berkaitan dakwaan perihal dagangan palsu berhubung kandungan petrol yang dibekalkan,” katanya.

Beliau juga mengingatkan semua syarikat dan pengusaha stesen minyak supaya memastikan tangki simpanan bawah tanah diselenggara secara berkala serta mematuhi standard keselamatan dan kualiti yang ditetapkan.
Hanif turut menasihati pengguna yang terjejas untuk menyimpan resit rasmi pengisian petrol serta laporan pemeriksaan bengkel sebagai dokumen sokongan bagi tujuan aduan dan membantu siasatan.
b43019705bef067e: COLOMBO: Sri Lanka suffered a nationwide electricity blackout on Saturday after the national grid tripped, possibly because solar power generation exceeded consumption, officials said.
The country was without grid power for more than two hours, with no clear timeline for when electricity would be restored.
State-run Electricity Distribution Lanka (EDL) said engineers were working to fix a fault affecting the entire grid, and suspected excess solar power had caused the breakdown.
Energy minister Anura Karunathilaka said authorities hoped to restore supplies "stage by stage".
"We request rooftop solar system owners to disconnect their systems until further instructions in order to support the restoration efforts," he said in a brief statement.
The entire grid shut down in February 2025, when solar power generation exceeded consumption on a bright, sunny Sunday. It took more than six hours to restore supplies.
Sri Lanka has an installed solar power capacity of just over 3,000 megawatts, while daytime demand ranges from 2,000 to 2,500 megawatts.
Tax concessions have encouraged consumers to switch to solar and sell their surplus electricity to the grid, creating imbalances that the utility provider is struggling to manage.
The government aims to increase solar power generation capacity to nearly 4,400 megawatts within three years — a 388% increase from 2024.
6acca130a34f3103: MACHANG: About 75 per cent of inmates in prisons nationwide are serving sentences for drug-related offences, with the proportion exceeding 90 per cent at Machang Prison, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said Malaysia had 41 prisons housing between 90,000 and 100,000 inmates, with drug-related offences accounting for the bulk of cases.

"Among the offences are those under Sections 15(1), 12(2) and 39 of the Dangerous Drugs Act," he told reporters after the Home Ministry's Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani programmes at Sekolah Kebangsaan Jambu Lawar here today.
Saifuddin said Pengkalan Chepa Prison was the most overcrowded prison in the country

He said profiling of drug offenders showed that those aged between 15 and 39 remained the largest group involved in drug abuse, while the growing trend among children below 15 was also a cause for concern.
He said the trend required more comprehensive preventive measures, including early education and greater parental involvement to keep young people away from drugs.
"The National Anti-Drugs Agency (Nada) has three main functions — education and prevention, enforcement, and rehabilitation — to address drug abuse.
"Public education efforts must be strengthened to raise awareness and encourage families to take preventive action," he said.
On the Kampung Angkat Madani programme, Saifuddin said several projects had been implemented at Kampung Gosong to improve facilities and residents' well-being.

Upgrading works had been carried out at Surau Kampung Gosong and Masjid Bilal, including improvements to prayer areas, toilets, bathrooms, ablution facilities, public address systems and other interior amenities.
"Lighting has also been installed at the village cemetery after residents informed us that burials sometimes had to be carried out at night," he said.
He said 14 houses had also been upgraded through cooperation with Akademi Binaan Malaysia, involving 10 individuals supervised by the Prisons Department and Rela members.
Saifuddin said the Home Ministry's 11 agencies were allowed to select a school and a village each year under the programmes.
The initiative had been implemented for three consecutive years, covering 33 villages and 33 schools nationwide.

"This is something we are proud of at the Home Ministry. From the north to the south, including Sabah and Sarawak, we have reached villages selected based on their potential to bring significant added value to local communities," he said.
9d373682d47e33b2: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari today denied allegations that the party orchestrated a khalwat case involving former minister Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad to undermine a political rival.
Amirudin, who is also Selangor menteri besar, said PKR had never discussed or arranged any plan, privately or publicly, to entrap political opponents, news outlet Harian Metro reported.
“We have many other things to do than arrange khalwat cases.
“That is not our job,” he told reporters after launching the Semarak Kasih Yayasan Selangor 2026 programme today.
He added that the party did not want personal matters to become the basis of political rivalry or debate.
Khalwat is an offence under Islamic law involving a Muslim man and woman who are not married to each other being found alone together in circumstances that may suggest improper conduct.
The allegations surfaced after the Selangor Islamic Religious Department detained two people in Petaling Jaya last Thursday to assist investigations into a suspected khalwat offence.

The department confirmed yesterday that a man and a woman had been detained at about 6pm in Petaling Jaya under Section 29 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995, but did name the people involved.

Nik Nazmi, a PKR member for almost 21 years till his exit in May, confirmed publicly earlier today that he was one of two people detained and apologised to his wife, family and his current party over what he described as a lapse in judgement.
Parti Bersama Malaysia has since announced that its 44-year-old co-founder is to be suspended three months from October 20 following the khalwat scandal.
7ca167498f37dcde: KUALA LUMPUR: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are expected to affect parts of the country until 6pm.

The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), in a warning issued at 3.15pm, said adverse weather conditions were forecast to affect the whole of Perlis, Kedah, Penang, Perak, Selangor, Melaka and Johor, as well as Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya.

The same conditions were expected in several areas of Terengganu (Hulu Terengganu, Dungun, Kemaman, Besut and Setiu); Kelantan (Gua Musang, Jeli, Tanah Merah and Pasir Mas); Pahang (Bentong, Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Jerantut, Kuantan, Pekan, Rompin and Maran); and Negeri Sembilan (Jelebu, Seremban, Port Dickson, Rembau, Kuala Pilah and Tampin).
In Sarawak, the affected areas were Kuching, Samarahan, Serian (Serian and Siburan), Sri Aman, Betong, Sarikei, Sibu (Sibu and Selangau), Mukah, Bintulu (Tatau), Kapit (Song), Miri and Limbang.

In Sabah, the warning covered Tawau, Kunak, Lahad Datu, the West Coast (Kota Belud, Putatan, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Penampang and Papar), the Interior (Beaufort, Sipitang, Tambunan and Membakut), Kudat (Kota Marudu) and Sandakan (Kinabatangan).
e97f621d463f5e40: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 17 — The Kuala Lumpur Immigration Department will investigate allegations of irregularities in the issuance of special passes at the Kuala Lumpur Immigration Office.
Its director, Datuk Hamsha Injau, said the department’s Integrity Division would conduct an investigation to determine the validity of the allegations and that no misconduct would be tolerated.
“Appropriate action will be taken if there is evidence of any breach of the law or regulations,” he said in a statement today.
He also advised the public to deal with the Immigration Department through official channels and avoid using unauthorised intermediaries.

A news portal reported today that special passes, which are intended to assist foreign nationals facing emergencies or urgent circumstances, were allegedly being systematically abused to extend their stay in Malaysia.

The report also alleged that the operation involved local intermediaries who handled applications, collected applicants’ passports and sent their photographs to immigration officers through messaging applications for preliminary verification. — Bernama
95abf91a6df1ed00: PETALING JAYA: VFive Group Sdn. Bhd. (VFive Group) terus memperkukuh reputasi dalam landskap perniagaan negara apabila dinobatkan sebagai antara 50 Perusahaan Mikro, Kecil dan Sederhana (PMKS) terbaik di Malaysia menerusi Anugerah Enterprise 50 (E50) 2026.
Pengarah Urusan VFive Group, Syafiq Abdullah, berkata kejayaan itu juga mengiktiraf prestasi perniagaan, keupayaan pengurusan dan daya saing syarikat.
Katanya, Anugerah E50 2026 turut mencerminkan komitmen dan usaha berterusan seluruh warga kerja dalam membangunkan sebuah organisasi yang berdaya saing serta mempunyai asas perniagaan yang kukuh.
“Sepanjang 14 tahun perjalanan VFive Group, kami melalui pelbagai fasa perkembangan dan cabaran yang membentuk keupayaan syarikat sehingga ke tahap hari ini.

"Daripada sebuah syarikat kecil, kami terus membina kepakaran, memperluas bidang perniagaan dan meningkatkan keupayaan organisasi untuk bersaing dalam persekitaran industri yang semakin mencabar," katanya.
Syafiq berkata pengiktirafan itu bukan sekadar pencapaian korporat, tetapi juga penghargaan terhadap komitmen seluruh warga kerja yang telah menyumbang kepada perkembangan VFive Group selama ini.

Pengiktirafan tersebut disampaikan oleh Menteri Pembangunan Usahawan dan Koperasi, Steven Sim pada Majlis Anugerah E50 2026 yang berlangsung di Renaissance Kuala Lumpur Hotel & Convention Centre malam tadi.

Diperkenalkan sejak 1997, Anugerah E50 merupakan antara platform berprestij di Malaysia yang mengiktiraf kecemerlangan syarikat tempatan berprestasi tinggi, berdaya saing dan berpotensi untuk terus berkembang.

Pemilihan penerima anugerah dibuat menerusi proses penilaian menyeluruh yang merangkumi kedudukan kewangan, pertumbuhan hasil, penerapan pendigitalan dan e-dagang, amalan alam sekitar, sosial dan tadbir urus serta pendekatan proaktif dalam pembangunan perniagaan.
Program ini dianjurkan oleh SME Corp iaitu agensi di bawah Kementerian Pembangunan Usahawan dan Koperasi.
1cdcffc32e52e17a: KUCHING: Tiada taman asuhan kanak-kanak (taska) diarah tutup setakat ini susulan keadaan jerebu, namun semua aktiviti luar perlu dihentikan bagi mengurangkan pendedahan kanak-kanak kepada udara tercemar.

Menteri Pembangunan Wanita, Keluarga dan Masyarakat Nancy Shukri berkata keputusan untuk tidak mengarahkan penutupan taska secara menyeluruh mengambil kira keperluan ibu bapa yang bergantung kepada perkhidmatan itu ketika bekerja.

Beliau berkata ibu bapa diberi budi bicara untuk menentukan sama ada mahu menghantar anak ke taska atau tidak, khususnya di kawasan yang sekolahnya telah diarahkan tutup susulan bacaan Indeks Pencemaran Udara (IPU) yang tinggi.
"Kami memahami ada ibu bapa yang tidak boleh membiarkan anak mereka di rumah begitu sahaja kerana tiada individu yang boleh menjaga mereka.

"Jadi, mungkin ibu bapa boleh berbincang dengan majikan atau pihak taska masing-masing mengenai langkah yang perlu diambil. Namun, perkara utama yang perlu dipatuhi ialah kanak-kanak tidak dibenarkan bermain di luar," katanya kepada selepas menyempurnakan program Empowerus 2026 bertemakan 'Empowering Leaders: Sustainable, Resilient and Ethical Leadership'.
Nancy berkata ibu bapa juga dinasihatkan supaya membawa anak mendapatkan pemeriksaan doktor sekiranya mereka menunjukkan gejala sakit ketika keadaan jerebu berterusan.
379ffd21dbeb36c7: SEREMBAN, Oct 17 — Police said preliminary post-mortem findings showed that pressure applied to the neck caused the death of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer found at a government staff quarters in Nilai.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the finding followed a nearly five-hour post-mortem examination that began at 9.40 am today at Tuanku Ja’afar Hospital here.
“The examination also found three stab wounds inflicted with a sharp weapon, two on the abdomen and one on the right cheek,” he said in a statement.
On October 15, the woman, who was in her 30s, was found dead at the quarters after she was believed to have been stabbed by her husband, reportedly following a misunderstanding.

Alzafny had earlier said police received a report about the incident at 9.30pm after the victim’s husband, also in his 30s, turned himself in at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang, Selangor, and reported her death.
He was subsequently remanded until October 22 to assist in the investigation under Section 302 of the Penal Code. — Bernama
c26747833ea5a3fd: MOSCOW: Russia's defence ministry said on Saturday it had carried out a large-scale overnight attack on Ukrainian infrastructure targets, including the country's largest steelworks in the city of Kryvyi Rih.
The plant is owned by steel giant ArcelorMittal, which suspended the facility's operations in September after a series of Russian ballistic missile strikes.
In a statement, the ministry said the plant supplied steel products to the Ukrainian military-industrial complex.
It said Russian forces had also hit an electricity substation in the northwestern city of Zhytomyr and another steel plant in Zaporizhzhia, a city near the front line.
A cargo vessel in the Black Sea was also hit, it said, alleging that it was delivering military cargo to Ukraine's Odesa port.
Reuters could not independently confirm the ministry's report.
8b41abed692c7963: KUALA LUMPUR: PKR will field a mix of seasoned and experienced candidates, young people and women from various ethnic groups in the 16th Melaka state election on Nov 14.

PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the party's candidates will be individuals capable of serving the community and possessing qualities that can help secure victory in the state constituencies they contest.

"In some state constituencies where our support is relatively low, we will allow candidates to gain experience. This is part of the party's and Pakatan Harapan's (PH) long-term plan," he told reporters after attending the Semarak Kasih event with Yayasan Selangor students today.
Asked about cooperation with other parties, Amirudin, who is also PKR election director, said a decision will be made within the next one to two weeks.

PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said yesterday that the party would contest nine seats in the Melaka state election, with its list of candidates to be announced by PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also PH chairman, on Oct 24.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state polls, with early voting on Nov 10 and nomination day on Oct 31.
Melaka has 28 state assembly seats, with Barisan Nasional (BN) winning 21 in the previous state election, PH securing five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) taking the remaining two.
82c7cb20d0e98828: PETALING JAYA: Men’s doubles shuttlers Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik are one step away from achieving their first World Tour title this year after qualifying for the final of the Denmark Open by defeating the world’s top pair from South Korea.

In what was anticipated to be the clash of the titans, the world No 4 pair surprisingly defeated Kim Won Ho-Seu Seung Jae in straight games of 21-14, 21-18 in 38 minutes at the SJF Bank Arena in Odense today.
They will face either Indonesian pair Fajar Alfian-Shohibul Fikri or China's Liang Wei Keng-Wang Chang in the final of the World Tour Super 750 championships tomorrow.
Aaron-Wooi Yik and Won Ho-Seung Jae have now won three matches each in their six encounters so far.
The Malaysians, who reunited for this tournament after a brief split to try new combinations, last beat the South Koreans in the semi-final at the World Championships in New Delhi in August.
They are still looking for their first World Tour title this year after finishing as runners-up in three top-tier tournaments – the Malaysia Open, the All England, and the World Championships.

Aaron was also a runner-up at the Taipei Open when he partnered Aaron Tai as part of the Badminton Association of Malaysia's experiment to find the best combinations for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

Meanwhile, the gallant run of mixed doubles pair Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing, who beat higher-ranked opponents in all their three earlier rounds, came to an end at the hands of China’s Feng Yan Zhe-Huong Dong Ping in the semi-final.
Yan Zhe-Dong Ping, the world No 1 mixed doubles pair, defeated the 51st ranked Malaysians 21-13, 21-13 in 36 minutes.
The winners in the doubles categories will take home US$70,300 (RM287,048) and the runners-up US$33,250 (RM135,766). The losing semi-finalists will receive US$13,300 (RM54,306).
5e7e46936708a8c1: KUALA LUMPUR: Universiti Malaya (UM) menafikan dakwaan bahawa tindakan tatatertib diambil terhadap seorang mahasiswa susulan persoalan dan pandangan yang disuarakannya pada sesi Sidang Kemuncak Pemimpin Muda Masa Depan Antarabangsa (iFUTURE 2026), baru-baru ini.
Naib Canselor Noor Azuan Abu Osman berkata universiti itu sentiasa menghormati hak mahasiswa untuk bertanya dan menyuarakan pandangan.

"Saya ingin menjelaskan bahawa tiada sebarang tindakan tatatertib diambil terhadap mahasiswa berkenaan. Sehubungan dengan itu, dakwaan yang tersebar mengenai perkara ini adalah tidak benar," menurut kenyataan.
Beliau berkata platform seperti iFUTURE 2026 yang diwujudkan oleh Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi (KPT) menjadi ruang penting bagi mahasiswa berdialog secara langsung dengan kepimpinan universiti.

"Bagi saya, perbezaan pandangan bukanlah suatu ancaman, sebaliknya sebahagian daripada budaya intelektual yang perlu terus dipupuk. Kita mungkin tidak sentiasa bersetuju dalam semua perkara, namun mahasiswa perlu diberikan ruang untuk bersuara dan didengari," katanya.

Sidang kemuncak tiga hari bermula 11 hingga 13 Okt itu menghimpunkan 1,231 pemimpin mahasiswa terdiri daripada 813 peserta Malaysia dan 418 delegasi antarabangsa dari 60 negara, bagi memperkukuh jaringan kepimpinan mahasiswa antarabangsa menerusi wacana intelektual dan libat urus strategik.
163a0a14c6587e66: PETALING JAYA: Two lawyers have urged the government to bring home convicted killer Sirul Azhar Umar from Australia to reopen the "unresolved" murder case of Mongolian national Altantuya Shaariibuu, who was shot and had her body blown up in 2006.
Former attorney-general Tommy Thomas said it would take only 30 minutes for Malaysia to ensure that Sirul could be extradited from Australia, where he fled in 2015.

"Malaysia just needs to give an undertaking to Australia that Sirul won't face the death penalty on his return. The foreign and home ministers and the attorney general must sit together and write a letter to their counterparts in Australia," Thomas said.

"It's as easy as that — a letter that can be written in half an hour. I think there is no political will. They'd rather it be part of history and want everybody to forget about it. But it can't be forgotten."

The Altantuya case captured headlines as details emerged linking the woman to Abdul Razak Baginda, an aide to then defence minister Najib Razak, speculation about her involvement in a submarine deal between France and Malaysia, and messages between Razak and Musa Safri, another aide to Najib.

Thomas and lawyer Sangeet Kaur Deo, who represents Altantuya's family, said Sirul's extradition would allow Malaysian authorities to verify claims about the killing that Sirul made in a statutory declaration while being held in detention by Australian immigration.

Speaking to satellite broadcaster Al Jazeera in a two-part documentary "Murder in Malaysia - Justice for Altantuya" aired today, Thomas and Sangeet said Sirul's claims in his statutory declaration — and those by his accomplice Azilah Hadri in a separate declaration — must be verified in order to reopen the case.
Thomas and Sangeet said the two men should face action for making false declarations if their claims were not true.

Sirul fled to Australia seeking asylum before the Federal Court sentenced him to death. His asylum application was rejected in 2019 and he was held in detention until 2023, when he was released into society; however, he could not be deported to Malaysia under Australian law that prevents deportation where the applicant will face the death penalty.
With Malaysia's mandatory death sentence repealed and Azilah's sentence commuted to 40 years, Thomas said there is no reason Sirul cannot be extradited.
No reply from the AG
Sangeet said she had written to the attorney-general but received no response. "It's their duty to reply,” she said.
If Sirul lied in his affidavit, action should be taken, she said. "And if he is right, something should also be done. My job is simply asking for it to be investigated," she told Al Jazeera.

She said all that Altantuya's family wants is for Malaysia and Australia to find a lawful path through the courts and diplomacy so accountability is finally served. "We must end the standstill, because the standstill is the injustice."

She said the most obvious question is why Azilah, a police commando, would take instructions from Razak who was not his superior. "That's a question that hasn't been answered and ought to be investigated."

Sangeet noted that Razak, whose abetment charges were dropped, had every opportunity during the hearing of a civil suit filed by Altantuya's father Shaariibuu to state on oath that the two men acted alone.
"He chose not to take it."
Text messages to Musa Safri
The documentary revealed text messages sent by Razak to Najib's security aide Musa Safri the night before Altantuya's murder.
At 9.35pm, Razak wrote: "Did you get my SMS about wanting to meet at DPM's office?" Three minutes later: "When will you be there? I can drop by in the morning. Tks."

Razak was suggesting a meeting at the office of the deputy prime minister (then Najib), said Americk Singh Sidhu, a lawyer for the late private investigator P Balasubramaniam who was engaged by Razak to watch Altantuya's movements before she was killed.
"Now, one wonders why and for what purpose. You have Musa organising Azilah and Sirul for Razak, but why involve the deputy prime minister?”

He believes files from the short-lived task force set up by Thomas in the 2018-2020 Pakatan Harapan government should be reopened, as interviews with 40 witnesses had been conducted relating to Sirul's 2019 statutory declaration.

"I think this is a case where the truth must emerge. The truth is the casualty here. Obviously there are vested interests, strong forces. For whatever reasons, they just don't want the truth to emerge, so there must be public pressure."

Altantuya's father, Shaariibuu Setev, a Mongolian professor, has travelled to Malaysia more than 20 times seeking justice for his daughter and vowed not to give up his quest to find the man who ordered the policemen to kill her.
In June, Mongolia's new prime minister, Nyam-Osoryn Uchral, acknowledged the torment and financial hardship Shaariibuu has endured and presented him with an apartment.
The full documentary can be viewed at Al Jazeera.
a7cf847d50805d31: PORT DICKSON, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Army (TDM) will review its standard operating procedures (SOP) following the arrest of a serviceman found with a pistol, dozens of rounds of ammunition and liquid suspected to be ketum at a camp in Kuala Lumpur.
Chief of Army Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman said the review was part of the army’s continuous efforts to improve existing procedures and address any gaps identified.

“The same applies to this case. We are constantly monitoring. Although an SOP is already in place, we are always looking at continuous improvement,” he told reporters after the Passing Out Parade of Young Male Soldiers Series 206/26, involving 1,485 soldiers, here today.
The event was also attended by Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman.
Azhan said the individual, who is in his 30s, was undergoing a six-month transition training programme and was scheduled to complete his service in three months.

“For your information, the individual is undergoing transition training before completing his service and is currently detained at Sungai Buloh Prison for the trial process and further action,” he said.
He added that TDM would extend full cooperation to the authorities, including by providing the necessary information on the case.

Meanwhile, Malek Razak said the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM) had its own procedures and investigation protocols for handling cases involving its personnel to ensure that all actions were taken in accordance with established regulations. — Bernama

ee51cb2e4d72cc07: If cinemas must run 20 minutes of adverts before a feature, they could at least be honest about it. Or, I have a better solution … Do you remember the last time you were lied to? 7f491fb78fd52845: Amazon wants to ensure you have a personal AI that you can carry with you anywhere, listening in on your conversations so it can remind you of key details – and give you personalized shopping recommendations, of course. The global online bazaar has unveiled two new AI-based products from Bee, a startup in wearable devices that it acquired last year in a deal said to be worth $300 million. Bee’s original product for Amazon was tried out and sort of given approval by friend of The Register Corey Quinn, Chief Cloud Economist at Duckbill, earlier this year. One new gizmo, Bee Frontier, is designed to be worn like a watch or one of those fitness trackers, although to our mind it looks more like you are wearing a doorbell. The other, Bee Eclipse, is a slimline and lightweight device about the size of a credit card that attaches to the back of your phone magnetically, like a limpet. Both are intended to listen in to your conversations and help you remember important details, like when you are meeting your friend for a pint later and at which hospitality outlet. The devices take note of the details you might otherwise forget, and then turn them into useful conversation summaries, to-dos and reminders, Amazon says. The pair of devices feature a single button to turn on or off, and a visible indicator that lights up when one is listening in and its AI is summarizing the conversation. When enabled, the eavesdropper gathers context from your conversations to provide insights and recommendations. Summaries of your conversations can be accessed via a Bee mobile app on iPhone or Android (linked via Bluetooth), or an all-new desktop app. These can be organized using templates for things such as lectures, or users can just review memories from the past few days to see what you discussed. The Bee devices pick up on trends or themes that recur, and recommend personalized goals and actions. That sounds alarm bells for us, as it suggests the AI is designed to get to know you, and what you like. Along with the new hardware, Bee has now gained the ability to connect to Amazon’s Alexa+ AI assistant and Amazon.com, which means that you can ask Alexa for a meeting summary - or get personalized shopping recommendations from Amazon based on what your personal earwig has gleaned. However, Amazon says that the latest Bee products respect user privacy, as audio is processed into insights in real time and not stored, while transcripts are encrypted and only the user can access them. Bee Frontier is claimed to have IP67 water resistance, up to seven days of battery life, and has a USB-C charging port. Bee Eclipse also has a USB-C port but is said to last for more than 21 days of use from a single battery charge. Both devices come in a choice of colors, with Bee Frontier available now for $74.99 and Bee Eclipse due to be available shortly for $99.99. ®
b0afaa347443b94c: HONG KONG: A factory worker in China has sparked rumours that he might be the long-lost younger brother of Hong Kong actor-singer Jordan Chan, after a video showing their striking resemblance went viral on social media.
But the man has since denied being adopted, putting a damper on the online theories.
The video, uploaded to Douyin on Oct 13, showed the worker operating machinery at a factory.
Wearing a red safety helmet and a white T-shirt, he caught viewers' attention because his face, expressions, and overall look closely resembled the 59-year-old actor.
Internet users soon pointed out several supposed similarities.
These included the worker's surname, Chen, and a distinct mark on his ear that people claimed matched Chan's.
Some also compared the worker's reported name, Chen Xianglu, with the name believed to belong to Chan's younger brother, Chen Xiaolu. But none of these details proves a family link.
The rumours picked up steam after Chan's past comments about his poor childhood resurfaced.
The actor previously revealed that his family struggled financially, and his parents eventually gave away their youngest son for adoption because they could not afford to raise all their children.
According to reports, Chan remembered seeing a notice asking for a healthy boy for adoption when he was a child collecting scrap.
He told his parents about it, which initially made them angry. But the family's desperate situation eventually forced them to go through with the adoption.
Chan reportedly felt lasting guilt over the incident.
The actor later thought about searching for his younger brother, but his father discouraged him.

His father feared that a sudden reunion might disrupt the life the boy had built with his adoptive family. Taiwanese media reported his father's words: "They worked hard to raise the child. What right do you have to disrupt their lives?"
As the rumours spread, the factory worker addressed the claims during a livestream on Oct 15.
He said he had never been adopted, had older brothers and sisters, and originally came from Fujian province. He also denied other online claims about his personal life.
Despite his clear response, the story continues to draw attention online, with many people still commenting on how much the two men look alike.
Neither Chan nor his wife, actress Cherrie Ying, has publicly commented on the matter.
No DNA test or official evidence has proven that the two men are related.

5ccedf2d69825183: KUALA LUMPUR: Men's doubles pair Aaron Chia–Soh Wooi Yik marked their reunion with a place in the Denmark Open final on Saturday.

faee0861609a5913: PETALING JAYA: Drug abuse among children under 15 is becoming increasingly worrying and requires more comprehensive prevention efforts, says home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
Saifuddin said those aged between 15 and 39 made up the largest group of people involved in drug abuse, based on their profiles, Bernama reported.
He called for earlier intervention to address the problem, including better education and greater parental involvement.

“Public education efforts must be strengthened to raise awareness and encourage families to take preventive action,” he told a press conference after a home ministry programme in Machang, Kelantan, today.
Saifuddin said Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu recorded drug-related case rates above the national threshold, based on figures per 100,000 population.
Pendang in Kedah recorded the highest rate in the country, followed by Kuala Krai, Kelantan.
Other districts identified were Tumpat, Tanah Merah and Bachok in Kelantan, as well as Besut in Terengganu, all of which recorded rates exceeding 1,000 cases per 100,000 population.

Saifuddin stressed that cooperation between his ministry, the National Anti-Drugs Agency (AADK), the police, and state governments was crucial to intensifying awareness and prevention programmes in the affected areas.
These efforts would include community outreach programmes to educate the public and raise awareness of the dangers of drug abuse.
Saifuddin said immigration depots nationwide were facing capacity pressures because of daily enforcement operations against undocumented migrants.
The depots had a combined capacity of about 20,000 people, but the steady influx of detainees had led to overcrowding.

He attributed the increase in detainees partly to the immigration department's efforts to map areas with high concentrations of foreign nationals, based on data collected and analysed from enforcement operations nationwide.
“The mapping exercise enables the authorities to identify areas frequently used by foreign nationals as settlements or gathering places.
“Those detained may include individuals without travel documents, those with expired passes, those who have misused their passes, or those with refugee status,” he said.
0c416e82096b5d89: KUALA LUMPUR: Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) has suspended its co-founder Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad from all official party activities for three months.
The decision follows his admission that he was detained by religious authorities on suspicion of khalwat (close proximity) in Petaling Jaya on Oct 15.
The suspension takes effect from Oct 20 until Jan 19, 2027.
Bersama president Syukri Razab said the party took note of Nik Nazmi's admission and viewed the matter seriously.
He said issues involving party leaders and members must be addressed appropriately to safeguard the party's integrity, credibility and public confidence.

"Bersama takes this development seriously and maintains that every issue involving the party's leadership and members must be handled appropriately to preserve the party's integrity, credibility and public trust," he said in a statement today.
Syukri said the suspension was necessary and reasonable.
However, he stressed that the decision did not diminish Nik Nazmi's contributions and commitment to the party since its relaunch in May this year.

Nik Nazmi, a former natural resources and environmental sustainability minister, earlier admitted that he was one of two people detained by the Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) on suspicion of khalwat in Petaling Jaya on Oct 15.
He said he was with a woman when Jais officers arrived but denied that they had committed any indecent acts.
"I admit that it was a mistake. As I also informed the Jais officer, we indeed did not commit any indecent acts that would raise suspicion," he said in an earlier statement.
Nik Nazmi said he and his friends had initially held a discussion at a studio in Brickfields, Kuala Lumpur, before continuing it in Petaling Jaya to review materials related to a project.
He said only he and the woman were present when Jais officers arrived.
He apologised to his wife, family, Bersama members and supporters over the incident, acknowledging that his lapse in judgement had affected the party.
He also pledged to cooperate fully with any legal proceedings and said he would accept any decision made by the party leadership.
Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad had confirmed the detention.
59675b52a6a6bd48: PORT DICKSON, Oct 17 — The Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) is reviewing allowances for its volunteer reserve personnel to encourage greater participation in training and strengthen the reserve force.

Chief of Defence Force General Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman said the review was aimed at boosting commitment among reserve force members and strengthening the manpower pool for the regular armed forces.
He said the current hourly rates of RM9.80 and RM8 were relatively low, having last been reviewed around 2022.

“We want them to participate actively in training and activities organised by their respective regiments. Active involvement also gives them additional points if they wish to join the regular force, making the screening process easier,” he told reporters after the passing-out parade for 1,485 recruits from the 206/26 Series of Male Young Soldiers Training here today. Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman was also present.
Malek Razak said an estimated 40 to 50 per cent of registered reserve personnel were inactive, including failing to attend training when called up.

Under existing policy, those who remain inactive for several months or years are removed from the membership list, he said, adding that this hindered efforts to maintain the Territorial Army as a reserve force.
“Our target is a one-to-one ratio between reserve personnel and regular armed forces personnel,” he said.
To improve participation, the MAF will diversify training methods, upgrade infrastructure and strengthen promotional efforts.

Malek Razak said graduates of the Reserve Officers Training Unit (PALAPES) were given priority to join the regular armed forces through the graduate officer recruitment scheme and could also receive additional academic credits.

“We believe it is a waste for them to undergo military training, particularly as officers, only to leave after completing their studies. We want them to become the next generation of officers in the regular service,” he said.

In a separate development, he said the Malaysian Battalion (MALBATT) would hand over some support assets to the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) following the planned termination of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) mission early next year.
The assets include generators, general-purpose vehicles and other equipment that would not need to be returned to Malaysia.

Earlier, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said 292 assets worth an estimated US$10 million (about RM42 million) would be handed over in stages until January 2027 for welfare, humanitarian assistance and peacekeeping efforts for local communities.

Malek Razak also urged young people to join the MAF, particularly in technology, artificial intelligence (AI) and information technology (IT), to support the modernisation of the armed forces. — Bernama
44250da08438053a: PORT DICKSON: The army will review its standard operating procedures (SOP) following the arrest of a serviceman found with a pistol, dozens of rounds of ammunition and liquid suspected to be ketum at a camp in Kuala Lumpur.
Army chief Gen Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman said the review was part of the army's continuous efforts to improve existing procedures and address any gaps identified.

The event was also attended by Chief of Defence Force Gen Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman.
Azhan said the personnel, who is in his 30s, was undergoing a six-month transition training programme and was scheduled to complete his service in three months.
"The individual is undergoing transition training before completing his service and is currently detained at Sungai Buloh Prison for the trial process and further action," he said.

Meanwhile, Malek Razak said the armed forces had its own procedures and investigation protocols for handling cases involving its personnel to ensure that all actions were taken in accordance with established regulations.
d8dec666a8f2f7b0: MACHANG, Oct 17 — Immigration depots nationwide are facing capacity pressures due to daily enforcement operations against undocumented migrants, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said.
He said the depots had a combined capacity of about 20,000 people, but the continuous arrival of individuals detained during enforcement operations had led to overcrowding.

The increase in detainees is also result of the Immigration Department’s mapping of areas with high concentrations of foreign nationals based on data collected and analysed from enforcement operations nationwide.
“The mapping exercise enables the authorities to identify areas that are frequently used as settlements or gathering places by foreign nationals.
“Those detained may include individuals without travel documents, those holding expired passes, those who have misused their passes, or individuals with refugee status,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution was speaking at a press conference after attending the Home Ministry’s 2026 Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School launch ceremony here today.

He said action against each category had to take into account the individuals’ respective status and legal position, adding that enforcement operations also involved other enforcement agencies and local authorities.
Meanwhile, Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu had been identified as the four states recording drug-related case rates above the national threshold, based on figures per 100,000 population.
Saifuddin Nasution explained that the assessment was based on data from four sources, using a calculation method that referred to international standards.
Pendang in Kedah recorded the highest rate in the country, followed by Kuala Krai in second place.
Other districts identified were Tumpat, Tanah Merah and Bachok in Kelantan, as well as Besut in Terengganu, all of which recorded rates exceeding 1,000 cases per 100,000 population.
The data would be used to identify areas requiring more targeted prevention and enforcement measures, he said.

Saifuddin Nasution stressed that cooperation between the Home Ministry, National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK), police and state governments was crucial to intensifying awareness and prevention programmes in the affected areas.
These efforts would include community outreach programmes to educate the public and raise awareness of the dangers of drug abuse. — Bernama
eb6c4c65e0589c1c: MACHANG: Police are completing their investigation into an incident involving Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Terminal 1 after the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) returned the investigation papers.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the A-GC requested several improvements to the investigation papers before deciding on the next course of action.
He said although the papers were initially submitted to the A-GC within a week, prosecution authorities required further clarification and additional investigative work.
"The police are still completing the investigation. The A-GC has stated that several improvements need to be made to the investigation papers.
"The investigation papers contain statements recorded from witnesses and all information gathered during the investigation before being submitted to the A-GC.
"The A-GC must be fully satisfied with the findings before making a decision. Usually, if it is not satisfied, it will return the investigation papers to the police for further action," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after the Home Ministry's Kampung Angkat Madani and Sekolah Angkat Madani programmes at Sekolah Kebangsaan Jambu Lawar here today.
Saifuddin added that police have been instructed to complete the investigation in accordance with the A-GC's requirements.
The A-GC returned the investigation paper to the police on Oct 8.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar previously confirmed the paper was returned to enable further investigation into the incident involving the MCBA director-general.

77295ea79cea01fd: PETALING JAYA: Pemimpin Bersama Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad direhatkan daripada sebarang aktiviti parti itu selama tiga bulan susulan pengakuannya ditahan Jabatan Agama Islam Selangor (Jais) kerana berdua-duaan di tempat tertutup dengan seorang wanita bukan muhrim.

fd193c52127cbff5: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor branch of the domestic trade and cost of living ministry is investigating 10 complaints of RON95 petrol allegedly mixed with water, causing damage to vehicles in several areas in the state.
The ministry's Selangor director, Muhamad Hanif Asa'ari, said they checked seven petrol stations yesterday in response to complaints and reports on social media.
Twenty-seven cans of RON95 petrol were taken from the stations for laboratory analysis by the chemistry department, he said in a statement today.
He said all the petrol stations possessed Controlled Scheduled Articles licences and licences issued under the Petroleum Development Act 1974.

Hanif also said a notice had been issued under Section 32 of the Trade Descriptions Act 2011 requiring petrol station owners to submit information and business-related documents to assist in the investigation.
"Strict action in accordance with legal provisions will be taken against any party found to be committing violations that jeopardise the interests and safety of consumers," he said.
a54998c028c598fd: MACHANG, Oct 17 — The trend of drug abuse among those under the age of 15 is increasingly concerning and requires more comprehensive preventive efforts, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said that based on the profiles of individuals involved in drug abuse, those aged between 15 and 39 formed the largest group.
He added that this development necessitates a preventive approach that also emphasises early education and the role of parents in curbing the involvement of youngsters in drug abuse.
“The National Anti-Drugs Agency (AADK) has three main functions, namely education and prevention, enforcement and rehabilitation, to address the issue of drug abuse.

“Efforts to educate the public must be strengthened to raise awareness and encourage preventive action among families,” he told a media conference after attending the Home Ministry’s Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School 2026 launching ceremony here today.

Meanwhile, commenting on the seizure of 521 kilogrammes (kg) of methamphetamine from a private jet in Laos recently, Saifuddin Nasution said the drugs were found aboard the aircraft before it was due to depart for Manila.
He said the aircraft had departed from Subang for Laos without any drugs on board, before the consignment was loaded into the plane when it was in that country.
“Laotian authorities detected the drugs when the aircraft was about to continue its flight to Manila,.
“Police have traced the aircraft’s owner, as well as its pilot and co-pilot, to assist in the investigation as the aircraft had departed from Subang,” he said.
He said investigation was also focusing on the party that charted the aircraft, the purpose of the charter and its intended destination.
Saifuddin Nasution said the aircraft owner’s identity had been established, but further details of the investigation could not yet be disclosed.

Previously, Lao police seized 521kg of crystal methamphetamine from a private Learjet that had arrived from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport, with 13 individuals arrested in connection with the case.

The Vientiane Times, quoting the Lao Security Newspaper, reported that the security operation was conducted on October 1 following information received by provincial police on Sept 21 regarding a drug trafficking syndicate believed to be planning to smuggle narcotics across the border by air, using a private aircraft.

According to the report, police subsequently received information about a change in the flight schedule, with the private jet expected to arrive from Malaysia at Luang Prabang International Airport at 1.30 pm on October 1. — Bernama
09f4f0f60444ee08: DUBAI: A tanker was struck by an "unknown projectile" off Saudi Arabia's Gulf coast, forcing the evacuation of its crew, a maritime monitoring agency said on Saturday.
The vessel was hit on Friday, 68 nautical miles off the coast of Jubail, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said, adding that "all crew are reported safe".
Ships have regularly come under Iranian fire during the Middle East war, as Iran blocks the Strait of Hormuz – the only exit route for oil and gas exports via the Gulf sea.
Vanguard, another maritime security agency, identified the ship as the Marshall Islands-flagged Safeen Principal crude oil tanker, saying it lost power and suffered an engine-room fire.
UKMTO later said that also on Friday, a ship in the same area was attacked by a rocket-propelled grenade, with the crew reported safe.
About one-fifth of global oil exports passed through Hormuz before the war began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb 28. Oil prices have soared during the war.

4896b284c5536883: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 17 — The legal team representing Noraidah Lamat, the mother of Zara Qairina Mahathir, has yet to decide whether to pursue civil action against any party, with its immediate focus on completing written submissions for the inquest.
Counsel Shahlan Jufri, speaking on behalf of the team, said the matter would be discussed with Noraidah before any decision was made on further legal action.

“For now, our focus is on the inquest, particularly the written submissions. We will discuss the matter with our client, as the final decision on whether to take civil action against any party deemed responsible rests with her,” he told a press conference after the inquest proceedings yesterday.
Shahlan also revealed that Noraidah had sent a brief WhatsApp message that morning, expressing her hope that everything would be made easier.
He thanked members of the media for their coverage of the inquest, describing it as professional, accurate and timely.
Shahlan said the 96-day inquest had been a challenging process, although it had proceeded relatively swiftly alongside proceedings in the Court for Children.
“There is a lot that we need to address in our written submissions, and we hope the decision eventually reached will be fair to all parties,” he said.
On the funds raised to support the inquest, Shahlan clarified that the amount collected was slightly more than RM200,000, dismissing claims that it had reached RM1 million or RM2 million.

He said the fund was announced by Senator Marhamah Rosli last year and had been independently audited after Noraidah and the legal team appointed a qualified independent accountant in April this year.
According to Shahlan, the money was intended solely to cover expenses related to the inquest and had not been used for other purposes.
He added that the legal team had handled the case on a pro bono basis, meaning no legal fees were charged.
Shahlan also said there was no legal requirement for Noraidah or the legal team to make the audit report publicly available. — Daily Express
768c5b134c4c2d56: The UK Space Agency needs a name for its Active Debris Removal Mission and has decided that the great British public are the people for the job. The agency confirmed the operation earlier this week and selected ClearSpace UK to lead it. The plan is to remove two UK-registered satellites from Low Earth Orbit, with the clean-up due to begin in 2029. The UK government is backing the effort with more than £60 million, and it expects the disposal to be completed by 2032. The spacecraft will grab each satellite, drop it into a lower orbit for disposal by burning up in the Earth's atmosphe, then climb to a higher one to await its next job. Less suicide dive, more cosmic bin round. And because it’s refuellable, the UK government says it "can help make a difference and sweep space for years to come." Launch is planned from SaxaVord Spaceport in Scotland. But first, the quest needs a name. The Active Debris Removal Mission hardly trips off the tongue, and the UK Space Agency gave inspirational examples of other project names, such as NASA's Mercury program (named after the Roman god) or Tim Peake's Principia mission (inspired by Sir Isaac Newton's Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica). Oddly, the agency didn't mention the poll to brand a scientific research ship, which was eventually named Sir David Attenborough rather than Boaty McBoatface, the most popular suggestion. The tag must consist of two words – so no "Itsy bitsy teeny weeny orbit debris clear machiney" – and 150 words to explain the name and how it reflects the theme. So no backronyms, for example Broom (British Robotic Orbital Object Manipulator). Starry McBinface? Obviously, swear words are not allowed, nor is anything deemed "potentially offensive" or political. Using anything that might attract copyright or intellectual property lawyers is also out. Letting the public suggest a name feels potentially riskier than the mission itself, though it should generate some engagement. It's a high-risk, high-reward campaign; there are plenty of dead satellites cluttering orbit, and the ability to remove them is becoming increasingly important. Rob Atchison, Managing Director of ClearSpace UK, said, "Our next step is to design, build and test a spacecraft that can get close, safely, to an object never designed to be caught, and take control of it." If you're getting a sense of déjà vu about this expedition, you're probably right. The European Space Agency (ESA) announced ClearSpace-1 in 2019, which the agency called "the first space mission to remove an item of debris from orbit" with a launch set for 2025. At the time, ClearSpace founder and CEO Luc Piguet said: "This is the right time for such a mission." In latest announcement, Piguet called the UKSA's selection "an important milestone." This is far from the first mission to grapple an object in orbit. Most recently, Katalyst Space sent its LINK spacecraft to rescue NASA's Swift observatory. That was intended to capture the Swift spacecraft and raise its altitude, but failures with LINK doomed it. Perhaps things might have gone better if the public had been given an opportunity to name the spacecraft? ®
